cc-antya-15.99.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

devanagari: वन्दे श्री - कृष्ण - चैतन्यं कृष्ण - भावामृतं हि यः ।
आस्वाद्यास्वादयन्भक्ता न्प्रेम - दीक्षामशिक्षयत् ॥1॥
cc-antya-16.1.translation: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who personally tasted the nectar of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa and then instructed His devotees how to taste it. Thus He enlightened them about ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa to initiate them into transcendental knowledge.

lines: uttama-vastu bheṭa lañā tāṅra ṭhāñi yāya
devanagari: ब्राह्मण - वैष्णव यत - छोट, बड़ हय ।
उत्तम - वस्तु भेट लञा ताँर ठाञि याय ॥10॥
cc-antya-16.10.translation: He would go to all the Vaiṣṇavas born in brāhmaṇa families, be they neophyte or advanced devotees, and present them gifts of first-class eatables.

lines: sei yāṅra haya, 'phelā' pāya sei dhanya"
devanagari: ‘सुकृति’ - शब्दे कहे ‘कृष्ण - कृपा - हेतु पुण्य’ ।
सेइ याँर हय, ‘फेला’ पाय सेइ धन्य” ॥100॥
cc-antya-16.100.translation: "The word 'sukṛti' refers to pious activities performed by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa. One who is fortunate enough to obtain such mercy receives the remnants of the Lord's food and thus becomes glorious."

lines: eta bali' prabhu tā-sabāre vidāya dilā
devanagari: एत बलि’ प्रभु ता - सबारे विदाय दिला ।
उपल - भोग देखिया प्रभु निज - वासा आइला ॥101॥
cc-antya-16.101.translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the servants. After seeing the next offering of food to Lord Jagannātha, a function known as upala-bhoga, He returned to His own quarters.

devanagari: मध्याह्न करिया कैला भिक्षा निर्वाहण ।
कृष्णाधरामृत सदा अन्तरे स्मरण ॥102॥
cc-antya-16.102.translation: After finishing His noon duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate His lunch, but He constantly remembered the remnants of Kṛṣṇa's food.

devanagari: बाह्य - कृत्य करेन, प्रेमे गरगर मन ।
कष्टे सम्वरण करेन, आवेश सघन ॥103॥
cc-antya-16.103.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His external activities, but His mind was filled with ecstatic love. With great difficulty He tried to restrain His mind, but it would always be overwhelmed by very deep ecstasy.

devanagari: सन्ध्या - कृत्य करि’ पुनः निज - गण - सङ्गे ।
निभृते वसिला नाना - कृष्ण - कथा - रङ्गे ॥104॥
cc-antya-16.104.translation: After finishing His evening duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with His personal associates in a secluded place and discussed the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in great jubilation.

devanagari: प्रभुर इङ्गिते गोविन्द प्रसाद आनिला ।
पुरी - भारतीरे प्रभु किछु पाठाइला ॥105॥
cc-antya-16.105.translation: Following the indications of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Govinda brought the prasāda of Lord Jagannātha. The Lord sent some to Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī.

devanagari: रामानन्द - सार्वभौम - स्वरूपादि - गणे ।
सबारे प्रसाद दिल करिया वण्टने ॥106॥
cc-antya-16.106.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then gave shares of the prasāda to Rāmānanda Rāya, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and all the other devotees.

lines: alaukika āsvāde sabāra vismita haila mana
devanagari: प्रसादेर सौरभ्य - माधुर्य करि’ आस्वादन ।
अलौकिक आस्वादे सबार विस्मित हैल मन ॥107॥
cc-antya-16.107.translation: As they tasted the uncommon sweetness and fragrance of the prasāda, everyone's mind was struck with wonder.

lines: aikṣava, karpūra, marica, elāica, lavaṅga, gavya
devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - “एइ सब हय ‘प्राकृत’ द्रव्य ।
ऐक्षव, कर्पूर, मरिच, एलाइच, लवङ्ग, गव्य ॥108॥
cc-antya-16.108-109.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These ingredients, such as sugar, camphor, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, butter, spices and licorice, are all material. Everyone has tasted these material substances before.

lines: kāhāṅ nā pāya, tabe rahe lukāñā
devanagari: ताँर ठाञि शेष - पात्र लयेन मागिया ।
काहाँ ना पाय, तबे रहे लुकाञा ॥11॥
cc-antya-16.11.translation: He would beg remnants of food from such Vaiṣṇavas, and if he did not receive any, he would hide.

lines: sei dravye eta āsvāda, gandha lokātīta
devanagari: सेइ द्रव्ये एत आस्वाद, गन्ध लोकातीत ।
आस्वाद करिया देख , - सबार प्रतीत ॥110॥
cc-antya-16.110.translation: "However," the Lord continued, "in these ingredients there are extraordinary tastes and uncommon fragrances. Just taste them and see the difference in the experience.

lines: āsvāda dūre rahu, yāra gandhe māte mana
āpanā vinā anya mādhurya karāya vismaraṇa
devanagari: आस्वाद दूरे रहु, यार गन्धे माते मन ।
आपना विना अन्य माधुर्य कराय विस्मरण ॥111॥
cc-antya-16.111.translation: "Apart from the taste, even the fragrance pleases the mind and makes one forget any other sweetness besides its own.

devanagari: ताते ए इ द्रव्ये कृष्णाधर - स्पर्श हैल ।
अधरेर गुण सब इहाते सञ्चारिल ॥112॥
cc-antya-16.112.translation: "Therefore, it is to be understood that the spiritual nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips has touched these ordinary ingredients and transferred to them all their spiritual qualities.

devanagari: अलौकिक - गन्ध - स्वाद, अन्य - विस्मारण ।
महा - मादक हय एइ कृष्णाधरेर गुण ॥113॥
cc-antya-16.113.translation: "An uncommon, greatly enchanting fragrance and taste that make one forget all other experiences are attributes of Kṛṣṇa's lips.

lines: sabe ei āsvāda kara kari' mahā-bhakti"
devanagari: अनेक ‘सुकृते’ इहा ह ञाछे सम्प्राप्ति ।
सबे एइ आस्वाद कर क रि’ महा - भक्ति” ॥114॥
cc-antya-16.114.translation: "This prasāda has been made available only as a result of many pious activities. Now taste it with great faith and devotion."

lines: āsvādite preme matta ha-ila sabāra mana
devanagari: हरि - ध्वनि क रि’ सबे कैला आस्वादन ।
आस्वादिते प्रेमे मत्त ह - इल सबार मन ॥115॥
cc-antya-16.115.translation: Loudly chanting the holy name of Hari, all of them tasted the prasāda. As they tasted it, their minds became mad in the ecstasy of love.

devanagari: प्रेमावेशे महाप्रभु यबे आज्ञा दिला ।
रामानन्द - राय श्लोक पड़िते लागिला ॥116॥
cc-antya-16.116.translation: In ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Rāmānanda Rāya to recite some verses. Thus Rāmānanda Rāya spoke as follows.

devanagari: सुरत - वर्धनं शोक - नाशनं स्वरित - वेणुना सुष्ठ - चुम्बितम् ।
इतर - राग - विस्मारणं नृणां वितर वीर नस्तेऽधरामृतम् ॥117॥
cc-antya-16.117.translation: "O hero of charity, please deliver unto us the nectar of Your lips. That nectar increases lusty desires for enjoyment and diminishes lamentation in the material world. Kindly give us the nectar of Your lips, which are touched by Your transcendentally vibrating flute, for that nectar makes all human beings forget all other attachments."

devanagari: श्लोक शुनि’ महाप्रभु महा - तुष्ट हैला ।
राधार उत्कण्ठा - श्लोक पड़िते लागिला ॥118॥
cc-antya-16.118.translation: Upon hearing Rāmānanda Rāya quote this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied. Then He recited the following verse, which had been spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in great anxiety.

lines: sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti jihvā-spṛhām
devanagari: व्रजातुल - कुलाङ्गनेतर - रसालि - तृष्णा - हर - प्रदीव्यदधरामृतः सुकृति - लभ्य - फेला - लवः ।
सुधा - जिदहिवल्लिका - सुदल - वीटिका - चर्वितः स मे मदन - मोहनः सखि तनोति जिह्वा - स्पृहाम् ॥119॥
cc-antya-16.119.translation: "My dear friend, the all-surpassing nectar from the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, can be obtained only after many, many pious activities. For the beautiful gopīs of Vṛndāvana, that nectar vanquishes the desire for all other tastes. Madana-mohana always chews pan that surpasses the nectar of heaven. He is certainly increasing the desires of My tongue."

lines: lukāñā sei pātra āni' cāṭi' khāya
devanagari: भोजन करिले पात्र फेला ञा याय ।
लुकाञा सेइ पात्र आ नि’ चाटि’ खाय ॥12॥
cc-antya-16.12.translation: After the Vaiṣṇavas finished eating, they would throw away their dishes or leaves, and Kālidāsa would come out of hiding, take the leaves and lick up the remnants.

lines: dui ślokera artha kare pralāpa kariyā
devanagari: एत कहि’ गौर - प्रभु भावाविष्ट हञा ।
दुई श्लोकेर अर्थ करे प्रलाप करिया ॥120॥
cc-antya-16.120.translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed by ecstatic loving emotions. Talking like a madman, He began to explain the meaning of the two verses.

lines: pāsarāya anya rasa, jagat kare ātma-vaśa,
devanagari: तनु - मन कराय क्षोभ, बाड़ाय सुरत - लोभ,
हर्ष - शोकादि - भार विनाशय
पासराय अन्य रस, जगत्करे आत्म - वश,
लज्जा, धर्म, धैर्य करे क्षय ॥121॥
cc-antya-16.121-122.translation: "My dear lover," He said, "let Me describe some of the characteristics of Your transcendental lips. They agitate the mind and body of everyone, they increase lusty desires for enjoyment, they destroy the burden of material happiness and lamentation, and they make one forget all material tastes. The whole world falls under their control. They vanquish shame, religion and patience, especially in women. Indeed, they inspire madness in the minds of all women. Your lips increase the greed of the tongue and thus attract it. Considering all this, we see that the activities of Your transcendental lips are always perplexing.

lines: āchuka nārīra kāya, kahite vāsiye lāja,
puruṣe kare ākarṣaṇa, āpanā piyāite mana,
devanagari: आछुक नारीर काय, कहिते वासिये लाज
तोमार अधर बड़ धृष्ट - राय ।
पुरुषे करे आकर्षण, आपना पियाइते मन
अन्य - रस सब पासराय ॥123॥
cc-antya-16.123.translation: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, since You are a male, it is not very extraordinary that the attraction of Your lips can disturb the minds of women. I am ashamed to say this, but Your lips sometimes attract even Your flute, which is also considered a male. It likes to drink the nectar of Your lips, and thus it also forgets all other tastes.

lines: sacetana rahu dūre, acetana sacetana kare,
tomāra veṇu śuṣkendhana, tāra janmāya indriya-mana,
devanagari: सचेतन रहु दूरे, अचेतन सचेतन करे
तोमार अधर - बड़ वाजिकर।
तोमार वेणु शुष्केन्धन, तार जन्माय इन्द्रिय - मन
तारे आपना पियाय निरन्तर ॥124॥
cc-antya-16.124.translation: "Aside from conscious living beings, even unconscious matter is sometimes made conscious by Your lips. Therefore, Your lips are great magicians. Paradoxically, although Your flute is nothing but dry wood, Your lips make it drink their nectar. They create a mind and senses in the dry wooden flute and give it transcendental bliss.

lines: veṇu dhṛṣṭa-puruṣa hañā, puruṣādhara piyā piyā,
'aho śuna, gopī-gaṇa, bale piṅo tomāra dhana,
devanagari: वेणु धृष्ट - पुरुष हञा, पुरुषाधर पिया पिया,
गोपी - गणे जानाय निज - पान ।
अहो शुन, गोपी - गण, बले पिडो तोमार धन ,
तोमार यदि थाके अभिमान ॥125॥
cc-antya-16.125.translation: "That flute is a very cunning male who drinks again and again the taste of another male's lips. It advertises its qualities and says to the gopīs, 'O gopīs, if you are so proud of being women, come forward and enjoy your property—the nectar of the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'

lines: tabe more krodha kari', lajjā bhaya, dharma, chāḍi',
nahe pimu nirantara, tomāya mora nāhika ḍara,
devanagari: तबे मोरे क्रोध क रि’, लज्जा भय, धर्म, छाड़ि’,
छाड़ि’ दिमु, कर आ सि’ पान ।
नहे पिमु निरन्तर, तोमाय मोर नाहिक डर ,
अन्ये देखों तृणेर समान ॥126॥
cc-antya-16.126.translation: "Thereupon, the flute said angrily to Me, 'Give up Your shame, fear and religion and come drink the lips of Kṛṣṇa. On that condition, I shall give up my attachment for them. If You do not give up Your shame and fear, however, I shall continuously drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. I am slightly fearful because You also have the right to drink that nectar, but as for the others, I consider them like straw.'

lines: āmarā dharma-bhaya kari', rahi' yadi dhairya dhari',
devanagari: अधरामृत निज - स्वरे, सञ्चारिया सेइ बले
आकर्षय त्रिजगत्जन ।
आमरा धर्म - भय क रि’, रहि’ यदि धैर्य ध रि’
तबे आमाय करे विड़म्बन ॥127॥
cc-antya-16.127.translation: "The nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, combined with the vibration of His flute, attracts all the people of the three worlds. However, if we gopīs remain patient out of respect for religious principles, the flute then criticizes us.

lines: nīvi khasāya guru-āge, lajjā-dharma karāya tyāge,
āni' karāya tomāra dāsī, śuni' loka kare hāsi',
devanagari: नीवि खसाय गुरु - आगे, लज्जा - धर्म कराय त्यागे
केशे ध रि’ येन लञा याय ।
आनि’ कराय तोमार दासी, शुनि’ लोक करे हा सि’
एइ - मत नारीरे नाचाय ॥128॥
cc-antya-16.128.translation: "The nectar of Your lips and vibration of Your flute join together to loosen our belts and induce us to give up shame and religion, even before our superiors. As if catching us by our hair, they forcibly take us away and surrender us unto You to become Your maidservants. Hearing of these incidents, people laugh at us. We have thus become completely subordinate to the flute.

lines: śuṣka bāṅśera lāṭhikhāna, eta kare apamāna,
nā sahi' ki karite pāri, tāhe rahi mauna dhari',
devanagari: शुष्क बाँशेर लाठिखान, एत करे अपमान ,
एइ दशा करिल, गोसाञि ।
ना सहि’ कि करिते पारि, ताहे रहि मौन ध रि’,
चोरार माके डाकि’ कान्दिते नाइ ॥129॥
cc-antya-16.129.translation: "This flute is nothing but a dry stick of bamboo, but it becomes our master and insults us in so many ways that it forces us into a predicament. What can we do but tolerate it? The mother of a thief cannot cry loudly for justice when the thief is punished. Therefore we simply remain silent.

devanagari: शूद्र - वैष्णवेर घरे याय भेट लञा ।
एइ - मत ताँर उच्छिष्ट खाय लुकाञा ॥13॥
cc-antya-16.13.translation: He would also take gifts to the homes of Vaiṣṇavas born in śūdra families. Then he would hide and eat the remnants of food they threw away in this manner.

lines: adharera ei rīti, āra śuna kunīti,
devanagari: अधरेर एइ रीति, आर शुन कुनीति
से अधर - सने यार मेला ।
सेइ भक्ष्य - भोज्य - पान, हय अमृत - समान
नाम तार हय ‘कृष्ण - फेला’ ॥130॥
cc-antya-16.130.translation: "That is the policy of these lips. Just consider the other injustices. Everything that touches those lips-including food, drink or betel-becomes just like nectar. It is then called kṛṣṇa-phelā, or remnants left by Kṛṣṇa.

lines: se phelāra eka lava, nā pāya devatā saba,
bahu-janma puṇya kare, tabe 'sukṛti' nāma dhare,
devanagari: से फेलार एक लव, ना पाय देवता सब
ए दम्भे केला पातियाय ? ।
बहु - जन्म पुण्य करे, तबे ‘सुकृति’ नाम धरे
से ‘सुकृते’ तार लव पाय ॥131॥
cc-antya-16.131.translation: "Even after much prayer, the demigods themselves cannot obtain even a small portion of the remnants of such food. Just imagine the pride of those remnants! Only a person who has acted piously for many, many births and has thus become a devotee can obtain the remnants of such food.

lines: kṛṣṇa ye khāya tāmbūla, kahe tāra nāhi rnūla,
devanagari: कृष्ण ये खाय ताम्बूल, कहे तार नाहि मूल
ताहे आर दम्भ - परिपाटी ।
तार येबा उद्गार, तारे कय ‘अमृत - सार’
गोपीर मुख करे ‘आलबाटी’ ॥132॥
cc-antya-16.132.translation: "The betel chewed by Kṛṣṇa is priceless, and the remnants of such chewed betel from His mouth are said to be the essence of nectar. When the gopīs accept these remnants, their mouths become like His spittoons.

lines: āpanāra hāsi lāgi', naha nārīra vadha-bhāgī,
devanagari: ए - सब - तोमार कुटिनाटि, छाड़ एइ परिपाटी
वेणु - द्वारे काँहे हर’ प्राण ।
आपनार हासि ला गि’, नह नारीर वध - भागी
देह’ निजाधरामृत - दान” ॥133॥
cc-antya-16.133.translation: "Therefore, My dear Kṛṣṇa, please give up all the tricks You have set up so expertly. Do not try to kill the life of the gopīs with the vibration of Your flute. Because of Your joking and laughing, You are becoming responsible for the killing of women. It would be better for You to satisfy us by giving us the charity of the nectar of Your lips."

lines: kahite kahite prabhura mana phiri' gela
devanagari: कहिते कहिते प्रभुर मन फिरि’ गेल ।
क्रोध - अंश शान्त हैल, उत्कण्ठा बाड़िल ॥134॥
cc-antya-16.134.translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was talking like this, His mind changed. His anger subsided, but His mental agitation increased.

lines: tāhā yei pāya, tāra saphala jīvita
devanagari: परम दुर्लभ एई कृष्णाधरामृत ।
ताहा येइ पाय, तार सफल जीवित ॥135॥
cc-antya-16.135.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "This nectar from Kṛṣṇa's lips is supremely difficult to obtain, but if one gets some, his life becomes successful.

lines: yogya hañā keha karite nā pāya pāna
tathāpi se nirlajja, vṛthā dhare prāṇa
devanagari: योग्य हञा केह करिते ना पाय पान ।
तथापि से निर्लज, वृथा धरे प्राण ॥136॥
cc-antya-16.136.translation: "When a person competent to drink that nectar does not do so, that shameless person continues his life uselessly.

lines: ayogya hañā tāhā keha sadā pāna kare
yogya jana nāhi pāya, lobhe mātra mare
devanagari: अयोग्य ह ञा ताहा केह सदा पान करे ।
योग्य जन नाहि पाय, लोभे मात्र मरे ॥137॥
cc-antya-16.137.translation: "There are persons who are unfit to drink that nectar but who nevertheless drink it continuously, whereas some who are suitable never get it and thus die of greed.

devanagari: ताते जानि , - कोन तपस्यार आछे बल ।
अयोग्येरे देओयाय कृष्णाधरामृत - फल ॥138॥
cc-antya-16.138.translation: "It is therefore to be understood that such an unfit person must have obtained the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips on the strength of some austerity."

lines: bhāva jāni' paḍe rāya gopīra vacana
devanagari: ‘कह राम - राय, किछु शुनिते हय मन’ ।
भाव जा नि’ पड़े राय गोपीर वचन ॥139॥
cc-antya-16.139.translation: Again Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Rāmānanda Rāya, "Please say something. I want to hear." Understanding the situation, Rāmānanda Rāya recited the following words of the gopīs.

lines: āmra-phala lañā teṅho gelā tāṅra sthāna
devanagari: भूडिमालि - जाति, ‘वैष्णव’ ‘झड़’ ताँर नाम ।
आम्र - फल ल ञा तेंहो गेला ताँर स्थान ॥14॥
cc-antya-16.14.translation: There was a great Vaiṣṇava named Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, who belonged to the bhūṅimāli caste. Kālidāsa went to his home, taking mangoes with him.

lines: gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur
devanagari: गोप्यः किमाचरदयं कुशलं स्म वेणुर् दामोदराधर - सुधामपि गोपिकानाम् ।
भुङ्क्ते स्वयं यदवशिष्ट - रसं ह्रदिन्यो हृष्यत्त्वचोऽश्रु मुमुचुस्तरवो यथार्याः ॥140॥
cc-antya-16.140.translation: "My dear gopīs, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips independently and leave only a taste for the gopīs for whom that nectar is actually meant. The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river, on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are standing like hair on her body."

lines: ei śloka śuni' prabhu bhāvāviṣṭa hañā
devanagari: एइ श्लोक शुनि’ प्रभु भावाविष्ट हञा ।
उत्कण्ठाते अर्थ करे प्रलाप करिया ॥141॥
cc-antya-16.141.translation: Upon hearing the recitation of this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became absorbed in ecstatic love, and with a greatly agitated mind He began to explain its meaning like a madman.

devanagari: एहो व्रजेन्द्र - नन्दन, व्रजेर कोन कन्या - गण
अवश्य करिब परिणय ।
से - सम्बन्धे गोपी - गण, यारे माने निज - धन
से सुधा अन्येर लभ्य नय ॥142॥
cc-antya-16.142.translation: "Some gopīs said to other gopīs, 'Just see the astonishing pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vrajendra! He will certainly marry all the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. Therefore, the gopīs know for certain that the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is their own property and cannot be enjoyed by anyone else.'

lines: kon tīrtha, kon tapa, kon siddha-mantra-japa,
devanagari: गोपी - गण, कह सब करिया विचारे
कोन् तीर्थ, कोन् तप, कोन् सिद्ध - मन्त्र - जप, ।
एइ वेणु कैल जन्मान्तरे? ॥143॥
cc-antya-16.143.translation: "My dear gopīs, fully consider how many pious activities this flute performed in his past life. We do not know what places of pilgrimage he visited, what austerities he performed or what perfect mantra he chanted.

lines: hena kṛṣṇādhara-sudhā, ye kaila amṛta mudhā,
devanagari: हेन कृष्णाधर - सुधा, ये कैल अमृत मुधा
यार आशाय गोपी धरे प्राण ।
एइ वेणु अयोग्य अति, स्थावर ‘पुरुष - जाति’
सेइ सुधा सदा करे पान ॥144॥
cc-antya-16.144.translation: “ 'This flute is utterly unfit because it is merely a dead bamboo stick. Moreover, it belongs to the male sex. Yet this flute is always drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, which surpasses nectarean sweetness of every description. Only in hope of that nectar do the gopīs continue to live.

lines: yāra dhana, nā kahe tāre, pāna kare balātkāre,
tāra tapasyāra phala, dekha ihāra bhāgya-bala,
devanagari: यार धन, ना कहे तारे, पान करे बलात्कारे ,
पिते तारे डाकिया जानाय ।
तार तपस्यार फल, देख इहार भाग्य - बल,
इहार उच्छिष्ट महा - जने खाय ॥145॥
cc-antya-16.145.translation: “ 'Although the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is the absolute property of the gopīs, the flute, which is just an insignificant stick, is forcibly drinking that nectar and loudly inviting the gopīs to come drink it also. Just imagine the strength of the flute's austerities and good fortune. Even great devotees drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips after the flute has done so.

devanagari: मानस - गङ्गा, कालिन्दी, भुवन - पावनी नदी ,
कृष्ण यदि ताते करे स्नान ।
वेणुर झुटाधर - रस, हञा लोभे परवश ,
सेइ काले हर्षे करे पान ॥146॥
cc-antya-16.146.translation: “ 'When Kṛṣṇa takes His bath in universally purifying rivers like the Yamunā and the Ganges of the celestial world, the great personalities of those rivers greedily and jubilantly drink the remnants of the nectarean juice from His lips.

lines: e-ta nārī rahu dūre, vṛkṣa saba tāra tīre,
devanagari: ए - त नारी रहु दूरे, वृक्ष सब तार तीरे,
तप करे पर - उपकारी ।
नदीर शेष - रस पाञा, मूल - द्वारे आकर्षिया ,
cc-antya-16.147.translation: "Aside from the rivers, the trees standing on the banks like great ascetics and engaging in welfare activities for all living entities drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips by drawing water from the river with their roots. We cannot understand why they drink like that.

lines: veṇure māni' nija-jāti, āryera yena putra-nāti,
devanagari: निजाङ्करे पुलकित, पुष्पे हास्य विकसित
मधु - मिषे वहे अश्रु - धार ।
वेणुरे मानि’ निज - जाति, आर्येर येन पुत्र - नाति
‘वैष्णव’ हैले आनन्द - विकार ॥148॥
cc-antya-16.148.translation: "The trees on the bank of the Yamunā and Ganges are always jubilant. They appear to be smiling with their flowers and shedding tears in the form of flowing honey. Just as the forefathers of a Vaiṣṇava son or grandson feel transcendental bliss, the trees feel blissful because the flute is a member of their family.'

lines: veṇura tapa jāni yabe, sei tapa kari tabe,
yā nā pāñā duḥkhe mari, ayogya piye sahite nāri,
devanagari: वेणुर तप जानि यबे, सेइ तप करि तबे ,
ए - अयोग्य, आमरा - योग्या नारी ।
या ना पाञा दुःखे मरि, अयोग्य पिये सहिते नारि ,
ताहा ला गि’ तपस्या विचारि ॥149॥
cc-antya-16.149.translation: "The gopīs considered, 'The flute is completely unfit for his position. We want to know what kind of austerities the flute executed, so that we may also perform the same austerities. Although the flute is unfit, he is drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. Seeing this, we qualified gopīs are dying of unhappiness. Therefore, we must consider the austerities the flute underwent in his past life.' "

lines: āmra bheṭa diyā tāṅra caraṇa vandilā
devanagari: आम्र भेट दिया ताँर चरण वन्दि ला ।
ताँर पनीरे तबे नमस्कार कैला ॥15॥
cc-antya-16.15.translation: Kālidāsa presented the mangoes to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura and offered him respectful obeisances. Then he also offered respectful obeisances to the Ṭhākura's wife.

lines: kabhu nāce, kabhu gāya, bhāvāveśe mūrcchā yāya,
devanagari: एतेक प्रलाप क रि’, प्रेमावेशे गौरहरि ,
सङ्गे लञा स्वरूप - राम - राय ।
कभु नाचे, कभु गाय, भावावेशे मूर्च्छा याय,
एइ - रूपे रात्रि - दिन याय ॥150॥
cc-antya-16.150.translation: While thus speaking like a madman, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became full of ecstatic emotion. In the company of His two friends, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya, He sometimes danced, sometimes sang and sometimes became unconscious in ecstatic love. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights in this way.

devanagari: स्वरूप, रूप, सनातन, रघुनाथेर श्री - चरण,
शिरे धरि करि यार आश ।
चैतन्य - चरितामृत, अमृत हैते परामृत,
गाय दीन - हीन कृष्णदास ॥151॥
cc-antya-16.151.translation: Expecting the mercy of Svarūpa, Rūpa, Sanātana and Raghunātha dāsa, and taking their lotus feet on my head, I, the most fallen Kṛṣṇadāsa, continue chanting the epic Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, which is sweeter than the nectar of transcendental bliss.

devanagari: पत्नी - सहित तेंहो आछेन वसिया ।
बहु सम्मान कैला कालिदासेरे देखिया ॥16॥
cc-antya-16.16.translation: When Kālidāsa went to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, he saw that saintly person sitting with his wife. As soon as Jhaḍu Ṭhākura saw Kālidāsa, he likewise offered his respectful obeisances unto him.

devanagari: इष्टगोष्ठी कत - क्षण क रि’ ताँर सने ।
झडु - ठाकुर कहे ताँरे मधुर वचने ॥17॥
cc-antya-16.17.translation: After a discussion for some time with Kālidāsa, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura said something to him in sweet words.

lines: kon prakāre karimu āmi tomāra sevana?
devanagari: “आमि - नीच - जाति, तुमि, - अतिथि सर्वोत्तम ।
कोन् प्रकारे करिमु आमि तोमार सेवन? ॥18॥
cc-antya-16.18.translation: "I belong to a low caste, and you are a very respectable guest. How shall I serve you?

lines: tāhāṅ tumi prasāda pāo, tabe āmi jīye"
devanagari: आज्ञा देह’, - ब्राह्मण - घरे अन्न लञा दिये ।
ताहाँ तुमि प्रसाद पाओ, तबे आमि जीये” ॥19॥
cc-antya-16.19.translation: "If you will permit me, I shall send some food to a brāhmaṇa's house, and there you may take prasāda. If you do so, I shall then live very comfortably."

devanagari: जय जय श्री - चैतन्य जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैत - चन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-antya-16.2.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of the Lord!

lines: tomāra darśane āinu mui patita pāmare
devanagari: कालिदास कहे , - “ठाकुर, कृपा कर मोरे ।
तोमार दर्शने आइनु मुइ पतित पामरे ॥20॥
cc-antya-16.20.translation: Kālidāsa replied, "My dear sir, please bestow your mercy upon me. I have come to see you, although I am very fallen and sinful.

devanagari: पवित्र ह - इनु मुइ पाइनु दरशन ।
कृतार्थ ह - इनु, मोर सफल जीवन ॥21॥
cc-antya-16.21.translation: "Simply by seeing you, I have become purified. I am very obligated to you, for my life is now successful.

lines: eka vāñchā haya,—yadi kṛpā kari' kara
pāda-raja deha', pāda mora māthe dhara"
devanagari: एक वाञ्छा हय , - यदि कृपा करि’ कर ।
पाद - रज देह’, पाद मोर माथे धर” ॥22॥
cc-antya-16.22.translation: "My dear sir, I have one desire. Please be merciful to me by kindly placing your feet upon my head so that the dust on your feet may touch it."

lines: ṭhākura kahe,—"aiche vāt kahite nā yuyāya
devanagari: ठाकुर कहे, - “ऐछे बात् कहिते ना युयाय ।
आमिनीच - जाति, तुमि सुसज्जन राय” ॥23॥
cc-antya-16.23.translation: Jhaḍu Ṭhākura replied, "It does not befit you to ask this of me. I belong to a very low-caste family, whereas you are a respectable rich gentleman."

devanagari: तबे कालिदास श्लोक प ड़ि’ शुनाइल ।
शुनि’ झडु - ठाकुरेर बड़ सुख ह - इल ॥24॥
cc-antya-16.24.translation: Kālidāsa then recited some verses, which Jhaḍu Ṭhākura was very happy to hear.

lines: sa ca pūjyo yathā hy aham
devanagari: न मेऽभक्तश्चतुर्वेदी मद्भक्तः श्व - पचः प्रियः ।
तस्मै देयं ततो ग्राह्यं स च पूज्यो यथा ह्यहम् ॥25॥
cc-antya-16.25.translation: "Even though one is a very learned scholar in Sanskrit literature, if he is not engaged in pure devotional service, he is not accepted as My devotee. But if someone born in a family of dog-eaters is a pure devotee with no motives for enjoyment through fruitive activity or mental speculation, he is very dear to Me. All respect should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted, for such devotees are indeed as worshipable as I am.'

lines: prāṇaṁ punāti sa kulaṁ na tu bhūri-mānaḥ
devanagari: विप्राद् द्वि - षडू - गुण - युतादरविन्द - नाभ - पादारविन्द - विमुखात्श्व - पचं वरिष्ठम् ।
मन्ये तद र्पित - मनो - वचनेहितार्थ - प्राणं पुनाति स कुलं न तु भूरि - मानः ॥26॥
cc-antya-16.26.translation: "A person may be born in a brāhmaṇa family and have all twelve brahminical qualities, but if in spite of being qualified he is not devoted to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a navel shaped like a lotus, he is not as good as a caṇḍāla who has dedicated his mind, words, activities, wealth and life to the service of the Lord. Simply to take birth in a brāhmaṇa family or to have brahminical qualities is not sufficient. One must become a pure devotee of the Lord. If a śva-paca or caṇḍāla is a devotee, he delivers not only himself but his whole family, whereas a brāhmaṇa who is not a devotee but simply has brahminical qualifications cannot even purify himself, not to speak of his family.'

lines: tepus tapas te juhuvuḥ sasnur āryā
devanagari: अहो बत श्व - पचोऽतो गरीयान् यज्जिह्वाग्रे वर्तते नाम तुभ्यम् ।
तेपुस्तपस्ते जुहुवुः सस्नुरार्या ब्रह्मानूचुर्नाम गृणन्ति ये ते ॥27॥
cc-antya-16.27.translation: "My dear Lord, anyone who always keeps Your holy name on his tongue is greater than an initiated brāhmaṇa. Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and therefore, by material calculations, be the lowest of men, he is glorious nevertheless. That is the wonderful power of chanting the holy name of the Lord. One who chants the holy name is understood to have performed all kinds of austerities. He has studied all the Vedas, he has performed all the great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas, he has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage, and it is he who is factually the Āryan.' "

lines: śuni' ṭhākura kahe,—"śāstra ei satya kaya
sei śreṣṭha, aiche yāṅte kṛṣṇa-bhakti haya
devanagari: शुनि’ ठाकुर कहे, - “शास्त्र एइ सत्य कय ।
सेइ श्रेष्ठ, ऐछे याँते कृष्ण - भक्ति हय ॥28॥
cc-antya-16.28.translation: Hearing these quotations from the revealed scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura replied, "Yes, this is true, for it is the version of śāstra. It is true, however, for one who is genuinely advanced in devotion to Kṛṣṇa.

lines: anya aiche haya, āmāya nāhi aiche śakti"
devanagari: आमि - नीच - जाति, आमार नाहि कृष्ण - भक्ति ।
अन्य ऐछे हय, आमाय नाहि ऐछे शक्ति” ॥29॥
cc-antya-16.29.translation: "Such a position may befit others, but I do not possess such spiritual power. I belong to a lower class and have not even a pinch of devotion to Kṛṣṇa."

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु रहेन नीलाचले ।
भक्त - गण - सङ्गे सदा प्रेम - विह्वले ॥3॥
cc-antya-16.3.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus stayed at Jagannātha Purī in the association of His devotees, always merged in ecstatic devotional love.

devanagari: तारे नमस्क रि’ कालिदास विदाय मागिला ।
झड़ - ठाकुर तबे ताँर अनुव्रजि’ आइला ॥30॥
cc-antya-16.30.translation: Kālidāsa again offered his obeisances to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura and asked his permission to go. The saint Jhaḍu Ṭhākura followed him as he left.

lines: tāṅre vidāya diyā ṭhākura yadi ghare āila
devanagari: ताँरे विदाय दिया ठाकुर यदि घरे आइल ।
ताँर चरण - चिह्न येइ ठाञि पड़िल ॥31॥
cc-antya-16.31.translation: After bidding farewell to Kālidāsa, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura returned to his home, leaving the marks of his feet plainly visible in many places.

lines: sei dhūli lañā kālidāsa sarvāṅge lepilā
devanagari: सेइ धूलि लञा कालिदास सर्वाङ्गे लेपिला ।
ताँर निकट एक - स्थाने लुकाञा रहिला ॥32॥
cc-antya-16.32.translation: Kālidāsa smeared the dust from those footprints all over his body. Then he hid in a place near Jhaḍu Ṭhākura's home.

devanagari: झडु - ठाकुर घर याइ’ देखि’ आम्र - फल ।
मानसेइ कृष्ण - चन्द्रे अर्पिला सकल ॥33॥
cc-antya-16.33.translation: Upon returning home, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura saw the mangoes Kālidāsa had presented. Within his mind he offered them to Kṛṣṇa-candra.

lines: tāṅra patnī tāṅre dena, khāyena cūṣiyā
devanagari: कलार पाटुया - खोला हैते आम्र निकाशिया ।
ताँर पत्नी ताँरे देन, खायेन चूषिया ॥34॥
cc-antya-16.34.translation: Jhaḍu Ṭhākura's wife then took the mangoes from their covering of banana tree leaves and bark and offered them to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, who began to suck and eat them.

lines: cūṣi, cūṣi, coṣā āṅṭhi phelilā pāṭuyāte
tāre khāoyāñā tāṅra patnī khāya paścāte
devanagari: चूषि’ चूषि’ चोषा आँठि फेलिला पाटुयाते ।
तारे खाओया ञा ताँर पत्नी खाय पश्चाते ॥35॥
cc-antya-16.35.translation: When he finished eating, he left the seeds on the banana leaf, and his wife, after feeding her husband, later began to eat.

devanagari: आँठि - चोषा सेइ पाटुया - खोलाते भरिया ।
बाहिरे उच्छिष्ट गर्ने फेलाइला लञा ॥36॥
cc-antya-16.36.translation: After she finished eating, she filled the banana leaves and bark with the seeds, picked them up and threw them in the ditch where all the refuse was thrown.

lines: sei kholā, āṅṭhi, cokalā cūṣe kālidāsa
devanagari: सेइ खोला, आँठि, चोकला चूषे कालिदास ।
चूषिते चूषिते हय प्रेमेते उल्लास ॥37॥
cc-antya-16.37.translation: Kālidāsa licked the banana bark and the mango seeds and skins, and while licking them he was overwhelmed in jubilation by ecstatic love.

devanagari: एइ - मत यत वैष्णव वैसे गौड़ - देशे ।
कालिदास ऐछे सबार निला अवशेषे ॥38॥
cc-antya-16.38.translation: In this way Kālidāsa ate the remnants of food left by all the Vaiṣṇavas residing in Bengal.

devanagari: सेइ कालिदास यबे नीलाचले आइला ।
महाप्रभु ताँर उपर महा - कृपा कैला ॥39॥
cc-antya-16.39.translation: When Kālidāsa visited Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed great mercy upon him.

devanagari: वर्षान्तरे आइला सब गौड़ेर भक्त - गण ।
पूर्ववत् असि’ कैल प्रभुर मिलन ॥4॥
cc-antya-16.4.translation: The next year, as usual, all the devotees from Bengal went to Jagannātha Purī, and, as in previous years, there was a meeting between Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the devotees.

devanagari: प्रति - दिन प्रभु यदि या’न दरशने ।
जल - करङ्ग लञा गोविन्द ग़ाय प्रभु - सने ॥40॥
cc-antya-16.40.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been regularly visiting the temple of Jagannātha every day, and at that time Govinda, His personal servant, used to carry His waterpot and go with Him.

devanagari: सिंह - द्वारेर उत्तर - दिके कपाटेर आड़े ।
बाइश ‘पाहाच’ - तले आछे एक निम्न गाड़े ॥41॥
cc-antya-16.41.translation: On the northern side of the Siṁha-dvāra, behind the door, there are twenty-two steps leading to the temple, and at the bottom of those steps is a ditch.

devanagari: सेइ गाड़े करेन प्रभु पाद - प्रक्षालने ।
तबे करिबारे याय ईश्वर - दरशने ॥42॥
cc-antya-16.42.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would wash His feet in this ditch, and then He would enter the temple to see Lord Jagannātha.

lines: 'mora pāda-jala yena nā laya kona jana'
devanagari: गोविन्देरे महाप्रभु कैराछे नियम ।
‘मोर पाद - जल येन ना लय कोन ज न’ ॥43॥
cc-antya-16.43.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered His personal servant Govinda that no one should take the water that had washed His feet.

lines: prāṇi-mātra la-ite nā pāya sei jala
antaraṅga bhakta laya kari' kona chala
devanagari: प्राणि - मात्र ल - इते ना पाय सेइ जल ।
अन्तरङ्ग भक्त लय करि’ कोन छल ॥44॥
cc-antya-16.44.translation: Because of the Lord's strict order, no living being could take the water. Some of His intimate devotees, however, would take it by some trick.

devanagari: एक - दिन प्रभु ताँहा पाद प्रक्षालिते ।
कालिदास आ सि’ ताहाँ पातिलेन हाते ॥45॥
cc-antya-16.45.translation: One day as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was washing His feet in that place, Kālidāsa came and extended his palm to take the water.

lines: eka añjali, dui añjali, tina añjali pilā
devanagari: एक अञ्जलि, दुइ अञ्जलि, तिन अञ्जलि पिला ।
तबे महाप्रभु ताँरे निषेध करिला ॥46॥
cc-antya-16.46.translation: Kālidāsa drank one palmful and then a second and a third. Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forbade him to drink more.

devanagari: “अतःपर आर ना करिह पुनर्बार ।
एतावता वाञ्छा - पूरण करिलुँ तोमार” ॥47॥
cc-antya-16.47.translation: "Do not act in this way any more. I have fulfilled your desire as far as possible."

devanagari: सर्वज्ञ - शिरोमणि चैतन्य ईश्वर ।
वैष्णवे ताँहार विश्वास, जानेन अन्तर ॥48॥
cc-antya-16.48.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the most exalted, omniscient Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore He knew that Kālidāsa, in the core of his heart, had full faith in Vaiṣṇavas.

lines: sei-guṇa lañā prabhu tāṅre tuṣṭa ha-ilā
devanagari: सेइ - गुण लञा प्रभु ताँरे तुष्ट ह - इला ।
अन्येर दुर्लभ प्रसाद ताँहारे करिला ॥49॥
cc-antya-16.49.translation: Because of this quality, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu satisfied him with mercy not attainable by anyone else.

lines: kṛṣṇa-nāma vinā teṅho nāhi kahe āna
devanagari: ताँ - सबार सङ्गे आइल कालिदास नाम ।
कृष्ण - नाम विना तेंहो नाहि कहे आन ॥5॥
cc-antya-16.5.translation: Along with the devotees from Bengal came a gentleman named Kālidāsa. He never uttered anything but the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: बाइश ‘पाहाच’ - पाछे उपर दक्षिण - दिके ।
एक नृसिंह - मूर्ति आछेन उठिते वाम - भागे ॥50॥
cc-antya-16.50.translation: On the southern side, behind and above the twenty-two steps, is a Deity of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. It is on the left as one goes up the steps toward the temple.

devanagari: प्रति - दिन ताँरे प्रभु करेन नमस्कार ।
नमस्क रि’ एइ श्लोक पड़े बार - बार ॥51॥
cc-antya-16.51.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His left side toward the Deity, offered obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁha as He proceeded toward the temple. He recited the following verses again and again while offering obeisances.

devanagari: नमस्ते नर - सिंहाय प्रह्लादाह्लाद - दायिने ।
हिरण्यकशिपोर्वक्षः - शिला - टङ्क - नखालये ॥52॥
cc-antya-16.52.translation: "I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. You are the giver of pleasure to Mahārāja Prahlāda, and Your nails cut the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu like a chisel cutting stone.

devanagari: इतो नृसिंहः परतो नृसिंहो यतो यतो यामि ततो नृसिंहः ।
बहिनृसिंहो हृदये नृसिंहो नृसिंहमादिं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥53॥
cc-antya-16.53.translation: "Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is here, and He is also there on the opposite side. Wherever I go, there I see Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. He is outside and within My heart. Therefore I take shelter of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead."

lines: ghare āsi' madhyāhna kari' karila bhojana
devanagari: तबे प्रभु करिला जगन्नाथ दरशन ।
घरे आ सि’ मध्याह्न क रि’ करिल भोजन ॥54॥
cc-antya-16.54.translation: Having offered obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Jagannātha. Then He returned to His residence, finished His noon duties and took His lunch.

devanagari: बहिर्द्वारे आछे कालिदास प्रत्याशा करिया ।
गोविन्देरे ठारे प्रभु कहेन जानिया ॥55॥
cc-antya-16.55.translation: Kālidāsa was standing outside the door, expecting the remnants of food from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Knowing this, Mahāprabhu gave an indication to Govinda.

devanagari: महाप्रभुर इङ्गित गोविन्द सब जाने ।
कालिदासेरे दिल प्रभुर शेष - पात्र - दाने ॥56॥
cc-antya-16.56.translation: Govinda understood all the indications of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Therefore he immediately delivered the remnants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's food to Kālidāsa.

devanagari: वैष्णवेर शेष - भक्षणेर एतेक महिमा ।
कालिदासे पाओयाइल प्रभुर कृपा - सीमा ॥57॥
cc-antya-16.57.translation: Taking the remnants of the food of Vaiṣṇavas is so valuable that it induced Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to offer Kālidāsa His supreme mercy.

lines: yāhā haite pāibā nija vāñchita saba kāja
devanagari: ताते ‘वैष्णवेर झुटा’ खाओ छा ड़ि’ घृणा - लाज ।
याहा हैते पाइबा निज वाञ्छित सब काज ॥58॥
cc-antya-16.58.translation: Therefore, giving up hatred and hesitation, try to eat the remnants of the food of Vaiṣṇavas, for you will thus be able to achieve your desired goal of life.

devanagari: कृष्णेर उच्छिष्ट हय ‘महा - प्रसाद’ नाम ।
‘भक्त - शेष’ हैले ‘महा - महाप्रसादाख्या न’ ॥59॥
cc-antya-16.59.translation: The remnants of food offered to Lord Kṛṣṇa are called mahā-prasāda. After this same mahā-prasāda has been taken by a devotee, the remnants are elevated to mahā-mahā-prasāda.

devanagari: महा - भागवत तेंहो सरल उदार ।
कृष्ण - नाम - सङ्केते’ चालाय व्यवहार ॥6॥
cc-antya-16.6.translation: Kālidāsa was a very advanced devotee, yet he was simple and liberal. He would chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa while performing all his ordinary dealings.

devanagari: भक्त - पद - धूलि आर भक्त - पद - जल ।
भक्त - भुक्त - अवशेष, तिन महा - बल ॥60॥
cc-antya-16.60.translation: The dust of the feet of a devotee, the water that has washed the feet of a devotee, and the remnants of food left by a devotee are three very powerful substances.

devanagari: एइ तिन - सेवा हैते कृष्ण - प्रेमा हय ।
पुनः पुनः सर्व - शास्त्रे फुकारिया कय ॥61॥
cc-antya-16.61.translation: By rendering service to these three, one attains the supreme goal of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. In all the revealed scriptures this is loudly declared again and again.

devanagari: ताते बार बार कहि , - शुन भक्त - गण ।
विश्वास करिया कर ए - तिन सेवन ॥62॥
cc-antya-16.62.translation: Therefore, my dear devotees, please hear from me, for I insist again and again: please keep faith in these three and render service to them without hesitation.

devanagari: तिन हैते कृष्ण - नाम - प्रेमेर उल्लास ।
कृष्णेर प्रसाद, ताते ‘साक्षी’ कालिदास ॥63॥
cc-antya-16.63.translation: From these three one achieves the highest goal of life-ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. This is the greatest mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa. The evidence is Kālidāsa himself.

devanagari: नीलाचले महाप्रभु रहे एइ - मते ।
कालिदासे महा - कृपा कैला अलक्षिते ॥64॥
cc-antya-16.64.translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala, and He invisibly bestowed great mercy upon Kālidāsa.

lines: se vatsara śivānanda patnī lañā āilā
devanagari: से वत्सर शिवानन्द पत्नी लञा आइला ।
‘पुरी - दास’ - छोट - पुत्रे सङ्क्ते आनिला ॥65॥
cc-antya-16.65.translation: That year, Śivānanda Sena brought with him his wife and youngest son, Purīdāsa.

lines: putra saṅge lañā teṅho āilā prabhu-sthāne
devanagari: पुत्र सङ्गे लञा तेंहो आइला प्रभु - स्थाने ।
पुत्रेरे कराइला प्रभुर चरण वन्दने ॥66॥
cc-antya-16.66.translation: Taking his son, Śivānanda Sena went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at His residence. He made his son offer respectful obeisances at the lotus feet of the Lord.

lines: 'kṛṣṇa kaha' bali' prabhu balena bāra bāra
tabu kṛṣṇa-nāma bālaka nā kare uccāra
devanagari: ‘कृष्ण कह’ बलि’ प्रभु बलेन बार बार ।
तबु कृष्ण - नाम बालक ना करे उच्चार ॥67॥
cc-antya-16.67.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the boy again and again to chant the name of Kṛṣṇa, but the boy would not utter the holy name.

lines: tabu sei bālaka kṛṣṇa-nāma nā kahilā
devanagari: शिवानन्द बालकेरे बह यत्न करिला ।
तबु सेइ बालक कृष्ण - नाम ना कहिला ॥68॥
cc-antya-16.68.translation: Although Śivānanda Sena tried with much endeavor to get his boy to speak Kṛṣṇa's holy name, the boy would not utter it.

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - ”आमि नाम जगते लओयाइ लुँ ।
स्थावरे पर्यन्त कृष्ण - नाम कहाइ लुँ ॥69॥
cc-antya-16.69.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I have induced the whole world to take to the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. I have induced even the trees and immovable plants to chant the holy name.

devanagari: कौतुकेते तेंहो यदि पाशक खेलाय ।
‘हरे कृष्ण’ ‘कृष्ण’ करि’ पाशक चालाय ॥7॥
cc-antya-16.7.translation: When he used to throw dice in jest, he would throw the dice while chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: इहारे नारिलुँ कृष्ण - नाम कहाइते !” ।
शुनिया स्वरूप - गोसाञि लागिला कहिते ॥70॥
cc-antya-16.70.translation: "But I could not induce this boy to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa." Hearing this, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī began to speak.

lines: mantra pāñā kā'ra āge nā kare prakāśe
devanagari: “तुमि कृष्ण - नाम - मन्त्र कैला उपदेशे ।
मन्त्र पाञा का’र आगे ना करे प्रकाशे ॥71॥
cc-antya-16.71.translation: "My Lord," he said, "You have given him initiation into the name of Kṛṣṇa, but after receiving the mantra he will not express it in front of everyone.

lines: mane mane jape, mukhe nā kare ākhyāna
devanagari: मने मने जपे, मुखे ना करे आख्यान ।
एइ इहार मनः - कथा - करि अनुमान” ॥72॥
cc-antya-16.72.translation: "This boy chants the mantra within his mind, but does not say it aloud. That is his intention, as far as I can guess."

lines: ei śloka kari' teṅho karilā prakāśa
devanagari: आर दिन कहेन प्रभु, - ‘पड़, पुरी - दास’ ।
एइ श्लोक क रि’ तेंहो करिला प्रकाश ॥73॥
cc-antya-16.73.translation: Another day, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to the boy, "Recite, My dear Purīdāsa," the boy composed the following verse and expressed it before everyone.

devanagari: श्रवसोः कुवलयमक्ष्णोर् अञ्जनमुरसो महेन्द्र - मणि - दाम ।
वृन्दावन - रमणीनां मण्डनमखिलं हरिर्जयति ॥74॥
cc-antya-16.74.translation: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is just like a bluish lotus flower for the ears; He is ointment for the eyes, a necklace of indranīla gems for the chest, and universal ornaments for the gopī damsels of Vṛndāvana. Let that Lord Śrī Hari, Kṛṣṇa, be glorified."

devanagari: सात वत्सरेर शिशु, नाहि अध्ययन ।
ऐछे श्लोक करे, - लोकेर चमत्कार मन ॥75॥
cc-antya-16.75.translation: Although the boy was only seven years old and still had no education, he composed such a nice verse. Everyone was struck with wonder.

lines: brahmādi deva yāra nāhi pāya sīmā
devanagari: चैतन्य - प्रभुर एइ कृपार महिमा ।
ब्रह्मादि देव यार नाहि पाय सीमा ॥76॥
cc-antya-16.76.translation: This is the glory of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's causeless mercy, which even the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā, cannot estimate.

lines: prabhu ājñā dilā sabe gelā gauḍa-deśe
devanagari: भक्त - गण प्रभु - सङ्गे रहे चारि - मासे ।
प्रभु आज्ञा दिला सबे गेला गौड़ - देशे ॥77॥
cc-antya-16.77.translation: All the devotees remained with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continuously for four months. Then the Lord ordered them back to Bengal, and therefore they returned.

lines: tāṅrā gele punaḥ hailā unmāda pradhāna
devanagari: ताँ - सबार सङ्गे प्रभुर छिल बाह्य - ज्ञान ।
ताँरा गेले पुनः हैला उन्माद प्रधान ॥78॥
cc-antya-16.78.translation: As long as the devotees were in Nīlācala, Jagannātha Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu maintained His external consciousness, but after their departure His chief engagement was again the madness of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: रात्रि - दिने स्फुरे कृष्णेर रूप - गन्ध - रस ।
साक्षादनुभवे, - येन कृष्ण - उपस्पर्श ॥79॥
cc-antya-16.79.translation: Throughout the entire day and night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu directly relished Kṛṣṇa's beauty, fragrance and mellow as if He were touching Kṛṣṇa hand to hand.

lines: vaiṣṇavera ucchiṣṭa khāite teṅho haila buḍā
devanagari: रघुनाथ - दासेर तेंहो हय ज्ञाति - खुड़ा ।
वैष्णवेर उच्छिष्ट खाइते तेंहो हैल बुड़ा ॥8॥
cc-antya-16.8.translation: Kālidāsa was an uncle of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī. Throughout his entire life, even in his old age, he tried to eat the remnants of food left by Vaiṣṇavas.

devanagari: एक - दिन प्रभु गेला जगन्नाथ - दरशने ।
सिंह - द्वारे दल - इ आ सि’ करिल वन्दने ॥80॥
cc-antya-16.80.translation: One day, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to visit the temple of Lord Jagannātha, the gatekeeper at Siṁha-dvāra approached Him and offered respectful obeisances.

lines: more kṛṣṇa dekhāo' bali' dhare tāra hāta
devanagari: तारे बले , - ‘कोथा कृष्ण, मोर प्राण - नाथ? ।
मोरे कृष्ण देखाओ’ बलि’ धरे तार हात ॥81॥
cc-antya-16.81.translation: The Lord asked him, "Where is Kṛṣṇa, My life and soul? Please show Me Kṛṣṇa." Saying this, He caught the doorkeeper's hand.

lines: āisa tumi mora saṅge, karāṅa daraśana'
devanagari: सेह कहे , - इँहा हय व्रजेन्द्र - नन्दन ।
आइस तुमि मोर सङ्गे, कराङदरश न’ ॥82॥
cc-antya-16.82.translation: The doorkeeper replied, "The son of Mahārāja Nanda is here; please come along with me, and I shall show You."

lines: eta bali' jagamohana gelā dhari' tāra hāta
devanagari: ‘तुमि मोर सखा, देखाह - काहाँ प्राण - नाथ?’ ।
एत बलि’ जगमोहन गेला ध रि’ तार हात ॥83॥
cc-antya-16.83.translation: Lord Caitanya said to the doorman, "You are My friend. Please show Me where the Lord of My heart is." After the Lord said this, they both went to the place known as Jagamohana, where everyone views Lord Jagannātha.

devanagari: सेह बले , - ‘एइ देख श्री - पुरुषोत्तम ।
नेत्र भरिया तुमि करह दरशन’ ॥84॥
cc-antya-16.84.translation: "Just see!" the doorkeeper said. "Here is the best of the Personalities of Godhead. From here You may see the Lord to the full satisfaction of Your eyes."

devanagari: गरुड़ेर पाछे रहि’ करेन दरशन ।
देखेन , - जगन्नाथ हय मुरली - वदन ॥85॥
cc-antya-16.85.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed behind the huge column called the Garuḍa-stambha and looked upon Lord Jagannātha, but as He looked He saw that Lord Jagannātha had become Lord Kṛṣṇa, with His flute to His mouth.

devanagari: एइ लीला निज - ग्रन्थे रघुनाथ - दास ।
‘गौराङ्ग - स्तव - कल्पवृक्षे करियाछेन प्रकाश ॥86॥
cc-antya-16.86.translation: In his book known as Gaurāṅga-stava-kalpavṛkṣa, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī has described this incident very nicely.

lines: kva me kāntaḥ kṛṣṇas tvaritam iha taṁ lokaya sakhe
tvam eveti dvārādhipam abhivadann unmada iva
drutaṁ gaccha draṣṭuṁ priyam iti tad-uktena dhṛta-tad-
bhujāntar gaurāṅgo hṛdaya udayan māṁ madayati
devanagari: क्व मे कान्तः कृष्णस्त्वरितमिह तं लोकय सखे त्वमेवे ति द्वाराधिपमभिवदन्नुन्मद इव ।
द्रुतं गच्छ द्रष्टुं प्रियमिति तदुक्तेन धृत - तद् भुजान्तर्गौराङ्गो हृदय उदयन्मां मदयति ॥87॥
cc-antya-16.87.translation: “ 'My dear friend the doorkeeper, where is Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of My heart? Kindly show Him to Me quickly.' With these words, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu addressed the doorkeeper like a madman. The doorkeeper grasped His hand and replied very hastily,'Come, see Your beloved!' May that Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rise within my heart and thus make me mad also."

devanagari: हेन - काले ‘गोपाल - वल्लभ’ - भोग लागाइल ।
शङ्ख - घण्टा - आदि सह आरति बाजिल ॥88॥
cc-antya-16.88.translation: The offering of food known as gopāla-vallabha-bhoga was then given to Lord Jagannātha, and ārati was performed with the sound of the conch and the ringing of bells.

devanagari: भोग सरिले जगन्नाथेर सेवक - गण ।
प्रसाद लञा प्रभु - ठाञि कैल आगमन ॥89॥
cc-antya-16.89.translation: When the ārati finished, the prasāda was taken out, and the servants of Lord Jagannātha came to offer some to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: गौड़ - देशे हय यत वैष्णवेर गण ।
सबार उच्छिष्ट तेंहो करिल भोजन ॥9॥
cc-antya-16.9.translation: Kālidāsa ate the remnants of food of as many Vaiṣṇavas as there were in Bengal.

lines: mālā parāñā prasāda dila prabhura hāte
āsvāda dūre rahu, yāra gandhe mana māte
devanagari: माला परा ञा प्रसाद दिल प्रभुर हाते ।
आस्वाद दूरे रहु, यार गन्धे मन माते ॥90॥
cc-antya-16.90.translation: The servants of Lord Jagannātha first garlanded Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and then offered Him Lord Jagannātha's prasāda. The prasāda was so nice that its aroma alone, to say nothing of its taste, would drive the mind mad.

lines: tāra alpa khāoyāite sevaka karila yatana
devanagari: बहु - मूल्य प्रसाद सेइ वस्तु सर्वोत्तम ।
तार अल्प खाओयाइते सेवक करिल यतन ॥91॥
cc-antya-16.91.translation: The prasāda was made of very valuable ingredients. Therefore the servant wanted to feed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu a portion of it.

lines: tāra alpa lañā prabhu jihvāte yadi dilā
devanagari: तार अल्प लञा प्रभु जिह्वाते यदि दिला ।
आर सब गोविन्देर आँचले बान्धिला ॥92॥
cc-antya-16.92.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tasted a portion of the prasāda. Govinda took the rest and bound it in the end of his wrapper.

devanagari: कोटि - अमृत - स्वाद पाञा प्रभुर चमत्कार ।
सर्वाङ्गे पुलक, नेत्रे वहे अश्रु - धार ॥93॥
cc-antya-16.93.translation: To Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the prasāda tasted millions upon millions of times better than nectar, and thus He was fully satisfied. The hair all over His body stood on end, and incessant tears flowed from His eyes.

lines: 'ei dravye eta svāda kāhāṅ haite āila?
devanagari: ‘एइ द्रव्ये एत स्वाद काहाँ हैते आइल ?।
कृष्णेर अधरामृत इथे सञ्चारिल’ ॥94॥
cc-antya-16.94.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu considered, "Where has such a taste in this prasāda come from? Certainly it is due to its having been touched by the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips."

devanagari: एइ बुद्ध्ये महाप्रभुर प्रेमावेश हैल ।
जगन्नाथेर सेवक दे खि’ सम्वरण कैल ॥95॥
cc-antya-16.95.translation: Understanding this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt an emotion of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, but upon seeing the servants of Lord Jagannātha, He restrained Himself.

devanagari: ‘सुकृति - लभ्य फेला - लव’ - बलेन बार - बार ।
ईश्वर - सेवक पुछे, - ‘कि अर्थ इहार’? ॥96॥
cc-antya-16.96.translation: The Lord said again and again, "Only by great fortune may one come by a particle of the remnants of food offered to the Lord." The servants of the Jagannātha temple inquired, "What is the meaning of this?"

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - “एइ ये दिला कृष्णाधरामृत ।
ब्रह्मादि - दुर्लभ एइ निन्दये ‘अमृत’ ॥97॥
cc-antya-16.97.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "These are remnants of food that Kṛṣṇa has eaten and thus turned to nectar with His lips. It surpasses heavenly nectar, and even such demigods as Lord Brahmā find it difficult to obtain.

lines: tāra eka 'lava' ye pāya, sei bhāgyavān
devanagari: कृष्णेर ये भुक्त - शेष, तार ‘फेला’ - नाम ।
तार एक ‘लव’ ये पाय, सेइ भाग्यवान् ॥98॥
cc-antya-16.98.translation: "Remnants left by Kṛṣṇa are called phelā. Anyone who obtains even a small portion must be considered very fortunate.

lines: sāmānya bhāgya haite tāra prāpti nāhi haya
kṛṣṇera yāṅte pūrṇa-kṛpā, sei tāhā pāya
devanagari: सामान्य भा ग्य हैते तार प्राप्ति नाहि हय ।
कृष्णेर याँते पूर्ण - कृपा, सेइ ताहा पाय ॥99॥
cc-antya-16.99.translation: "One who is only ordinarily fortunate cannot obtain such mercy. Only persons who have the full mercy of Kṛṣṇa can receive such remnants.

devanagari: लिख्य ते श्रील - गौरेन्दोरत्यद्भुतमलौकिकम् ।
यैदृष्टं तन्मुखाच्छ्रुत्वा दिव्योन्माद - विचेष्टितम् ॥1॥
cc-antya-17.1.translation: I am simply trying to write about Lord Gauracandra's transcendental activities and spiritual madness, which are very wonderful and uncommon. I dare to write of them only because I have heard from the mouths of those who have personally seen the Lord's activities.

devanagari: आचम्बिते शुनेन प्रभु कृष्ण - वेणु - गान ।
भावावेशे प्रभु ताहाँ करिला प्रयाण ॥10॥
cc-antya-17.10.translation: Suddenly, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute. Then, in ecstasy, He began to depart to see Lord Kṛṣṇa.

lines: tina-dvāre kapāṭa aiche āche ta' lāgiyā
devanagari: तिन - द्वारे कपाट ऐछे आछे त’ लागिया ।
भावावेशे प्रभु गेला बाहिर ह ञा ॥11॥
cc-antya-17.11.translation: All three doors were fastened as usual, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, in great ecstasy, nevertheless got out of the room and left the house.

lines: tāhāṅ yāi' paḍilā prabhu hañā acetana
devanagari: सिंह - द्वार - दक्षिणे आछे तैलङ्गी - गाभी - गण ।
ताहाँ याइ’ पड़िला प्रभु हञा अचेतन ॥12॥
cc-antya-17.12.translation: He went to a cow shed on the southern side of the Siṁha-dvāra. There the Lord fell down unconscious among cows from the district of Tailaṅga.

lines: ethā govinda mahāprabhura śabda nā pāñā
devanagari: एथा गोविन्द महाप्रभुर शब्द ना पाञा ।
स्वरूपेरे बोलाइल कपाट खुलिया ॥13॥
cc-antya-17.13.translation: Meanwhile, not hearing any sounds from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Govinda immediately sent for Svarūpa Dāmodara and opened the doors.

devanagari: तबे स्वरूप - गोसाञि सङ्गे लञा भक्त - गण ।
देउटि ज्वालिया करेन प्रभुर अन्वेषण ॥14॥
cc-antya-17.14.translation: Then Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī lit a torch, and went out with all the devotees to search for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: इति - उति अन्वेषिया सिंह - द्वारे गेला ।
गाभी - गण - मध्ये याइ’ प्रभुरे पाइला ॥15॥
cc-antya-17.15.translation: After searching here and there, they finally came to the cow shed near the Siṁha-dvāra. There they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lying unconscious among the cows.

devanagari: पेटेर भितर हस्त - पद - कूर्मेर आकार ।
मुखे फेन, पुलकाङ्ग, नेत्रे अश्रु - धार ॥16॥
cc-antya-17.16.translation: His arms and legs had entered the trunk of His body, exactly like those of a tortoise. His mouth was foaming, there were eruptions on His body, and tears flowed from His eyes.

devanagari: अचेतन पड़ियाछेन , - येन कुष्माण्ड - फल ।
बाहिरे जड़िमा, अन्तरे आनन्द - विह्वल ॥17॥
cc-antya-17.17.translation: As the Lord lay there unconscious, His body resembled a large pumpkin. Externally He was completely inert, but within He felt overwhelming transcendental bliss.

lines: gābhī saba caudike śuṅke prabhura śrī-aṅga
dūra kaile nāhi chāḍe prabhura śrī-aṅga-saṅga
devanagari: गाभी सब चौदिके शुङ्के प्रभुर श्री - अङ्ग ।
दूर कैले नाहि छाड़े प्रभुर श्री - अङ्ग - सङ्ग ॥18॥
cc-antya-17.18.translation: All the cows around the Lord were sniffing His transcendental body. When the devotees tried to check them, they refused to give up their association with the transcendental body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

lines: aneka karilā yatna, nā haya cetana
devanagari: अनेक करिला यत्न, ना हय चेतन ।
प्रभुरे उठाञा घरे आनिला भक्त - गण ॥19॥
cc-antya-17.19.translation: The devotees tried to rouse the Lord by various means, but His consciousness did not return. Therefore they all lifted Him and brought Him back home.

devanagari: जय जय श्री - चैतन्य जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैत - चन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-antya-17.2.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of the Lord!

devanagari: उच्च क रि’ श्रवणे करे नाम - सङ्कीर्तन ।
अनेक - क्षणे महाप्रभु पाइला चेतन ॥20॥
cc-antya-17.20.translation: All the devotees began to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra very loudly, and after a considerable time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained consciousness.

devanagari: चेतन ह - इले हस्त - पाद बाहिरे आइल ।
पूर्ववत् यथा - योग्य शरीर ह - इल ॥21॥
cc-antya-17.21.translation: When He regained consciousness, His arms and legs came out of His body, and His whole body returned to normal.

devanagari: उठिया वसिलेन प्रभु, चाहेन इति - उति ।
स्वरूपे कहेन , - “तुमि आमा आनिला कति ? ॥22॥
cc-antya-17.22.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stood up, and then sat down again. Looking here and there, He inquired from Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Where have you brought Me?

devanagari: वेणु - शब्द शुनि’ आमि गेलाङवृन्दावन ।
देखि, - गोष्ठे वेणु बाजाय व्रजेन्द्र - नन्दन ॥23॥
cc-antya-17.23.translation: "After hearing the vibration of a flute, I went to Vṛndāvana, and there I saw that Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda, was playing on His flute in the pasturing grounds.

devanagari: सङ्केत - वेणु - नादे राधा आ नि’ कुञ्ज - घरे ।
कुञ्जेरे चलिला कृष्ण क्रीड़ा करिबारे ॥24॥
cc-antya-17.24.translation: "He brought Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to a bower by signaling with His flute. Then He entered within that bower to perform pastimes with Her.

lines: tāṅra pāche pāche āmi karinu gamana
devanagari: ताँर पाछे पाछे आमि करिनु गमन ।
ताँर भूषा - ध्वनिते आमार हरिल श्रवण ॥25॥
cc-antya-17.25.translation: "I entered the bower just behind Kṛṣṇa, My ears captivated by the sound of His ornaments.

devanagari: गोपी - गण - सह विहार, हास, परिहास ।
कण्ठ - ध्वनि - उक्ति शुनि’ मोर कर्णोल्लास ॥26॥
cc-antya-17.26.translation: "I saw Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs enjoying all kinds of pastimes while laughing and joking together. Hearing their vocal expressions enhanced the joy of My ears.

lines: āmā iṅhā lañā āilā balātkāra kari'
devanagari: हेन - काले तुमि - सब कोलाहल क रि’ ।
आमा इँहा ल ञा आइला बलात्कार क रि’ ॥27॥
cc-antya-17.27.translation: "Just then, all of you made a tumultuous sound and brought Me back here by force.

lines: śunite nā pāinu sei amṛta-sama vāṇī
devanagari: शुनिते ना पाइनु सेइ अमृत - सम वाणी ।
शुनिते ना पाइनु भूषण - मुरलीर ध्वनि” ॥28॥
cc-antya-17.28.translation: "Because you brought Me back here, I could no longer hear the nectarean voices of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs, nor could I hear the sounds of their ornaments or the flute."

devanagari: भावावेशे स्वरूपे कहेन गद्गद - वाणी ।
‘कर्ण तृष्णाय मरे, पड़ रसायन, शुनि’ ॥29॥
cc-antya-17.29.translation: In great ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Svarūpa Dāmodara in a faltering voice, "My ears are dying of thirst. Please recite something to quench this thirst. Let me hear it."

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु रात्रि - दिवसे ।
उन्मादेर चेष्टा, प्रलाप करे प्रेमावेशे ॥3॥
cc-antya-17.3.translation: Absorbed in ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu acted and talked like a madman day and night.

devanagari: स्वरूप - गोसाञि प्रभुर भाव जानिया ।
भागवतेर श्लोक पड़े मधुर करिया ॥30॥
cc-antya-17.30.translation: Understanding the ecstatic emotions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara, in a sweet voice, recited the following verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

devanagari: का स्त्र्यङ्ग ते कल - पदामृत - वेणु - गीत - सम्मोहितार्य - चरितान्न चलेत्रि - लोक्याम् ।
त्रैलोक्य - सौभगमिदं च निरीक्ष्य रूपं यद्गो - द्विज - द्रुम - मृगाः पुलकान्यबिभ्रन् ॥31॥
cc-antya-17.31.translation: “ 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, where is that woman within the three worlds who cannot be captivated by the rhythms of the sweet songs coming from Your wonderful flute? Who cannot fall down from the path of chastity in this way? Your beauty is the most sublime within the three worlds. Upon seeing Your beauty, even cows, birds, animals and trees in the forest are stunned in jubilation.'

devanagari: शुनि’ प्रभु गोपी - भावे आविष्ट ह - इला ।
भागवतेर श्लोकेर अर्थ करिते लागिला ॥32॥
cc-antya-17.32.translation: Upon hearing this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, overwhelmed with the ecstasy of the gopīs, began to explain it.

lines: kṛṣṇera mukha-hāsya-vāṇī, tyāge tāhā satya māni',
devanagari: हैल गोपी - भावावेश, कैल रासे परवेश
कृष्णेर शुनि’ उपेक्षा - वचन ।
कृष्णेर मुख - हास्य - वाणी, त्यागे ताहा सत्य मा नि’
रोषे कृष्णे देन ओलाहन ॥33॥
cc-antya-17.33.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The gopīs entered the arena of the rāsa dance in ecstasy, but after hearing Kṛṣṇa's words of negligence and detachment, they understood that He was going to renounce them. Thus they began to chastise Him in anger.

lines: ei trijagat bhari', āche yata yogyā nāri,
devanagari: “नागर, कह, तुमि करिया निश्चय
एइ त्रिजगत् भरि’, आछे यत योग्या नारि, ।
तोमार वेणु काहाँ ना आकर्षय? ॥34॥
cc-antya-17.34.translation: “ 'O dear lover,' " they said, " 'please answer just one question. Who among all the youthful women within this universe is not attracted by the sound of Your flute?

devanagari: कैला जगते वेणु - ध्वनि, सिद्ध - मन्त्रा योगिनी
दूती हञा मोहे नारी - मन ।
महोत्कण्ठा बाड़ा ञा, आर्य - पथ छाड़ा ञा,
आनि’ तोमाय करे समर्पण ॥35॥
cc-antya-17.35.translation: “ 'When You play Your flute, it acts like a messenger in the form of a yoginī perfect in the art of chanting mantras. This messenger enchants all the women in the universe and attracts them to You. Then she increases their great anxiety and induces them to give up the regulative principle of obeying superiors. Finally, she forcibly brings them to You to surrender in amorous love.

lines: ebe āmāya kari' roṣa, kahi' pati-tyāge 'doṣa',
devanagari: धर्म छाड़ाय वेणु - द्वारे, हाने कटाक्ष - काम - शरे,
लज्जा, भय, सकल छाड़ाय ।
एबे आमाय क रि’ रोष, कहि’ पति - त्यागे ‘दोष’,
धार्मिक ह ञा धर्म शिखाय! ॥36॥
cc-antya-17.36.translation: “ 'The vibration of Your flute, accompanied by Your glance, which pierces us forcibly with the arrows of lust, induces us to ignore the regulative principles of religious life. Thus we become excited by lusty desires and come to You, giving up all shame and fear. But now You are angry with us. You are finding fault with our violating religious principles and leaving our homes and husbands. And as You instruct us about religious principles, we become helpless.

lines: tumi jāna parihāsa, haya nārīra sarva-nāśa,
devanagari: अन्य - कथा, अन्य - मन, बाहिरे अन्य आचरण ,
एइ सब शठ - परिपाटी ।
तुमि जान परिहास, हय नारीर सर्व - नाश,
छाड़ एइ सब कुटीनाटी ॥37॥
cc-antya-17.37.translation: “ 'We know that this is all a well-planned trick. You know how to make jokes that cause the complete annihilation of women, but we can understand that Your real mind, words and behavior are different. Therefore please give up all these clever tricks.

lines: tina amṛte hare kāṇa, hare mana, hare prāṇa,
devanagari: वेणु - नाद अमृत - घोले, अमृत - समान मिठा बोले ,
अमृत - समान भूषण - शिञ्जित ।
तिन अमृते हरे काण, हरे मन, हरे प्राण ,
केमने नारी धरिबेक चित ?” ॥38॥
cc-antya-17.38.translation: “ 'The nectarean buttermilk of Your flute's vibration, the nectar of Your sweet words and the nectarean sound of Your ornaments mix together to attract our ears, minds and lives. In this way You are killing us.' "

lines: eta kahi' krodhāveśe, bhāvera taraṅge bhāse,
devanagari: एत कहि’ क्रोधावेशे, भावेर तरङ्गे भासे
उत्कण्ठा - सागरे डुबे मन ।
राधार उत्कण्ठा - वाणी, पड़ि’ आपने वाखानि
कृष्ण - माधुर्य करे आस्वादन ॥39॥
cc-antya-17.39.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke these words in a mood of anger as He floated on waves of ecstatic love. Merged in an ocean of anxiety, He recited a verse spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī expressing the same emotion. Then He personally explained the verse and thus tasted the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: एक - दिन प्रभु स्वरूप - रामानन्द - सङ्गे ।
अर्ध - रात्रि गोडाइला कृष्ण - कथा - रङ्गे ॥4॥
cc-antya-17.4.translation: In the company of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu once passed half the night talking about the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

lines: sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti karṇa-spṛhām
devanagari: नदज्जलद - निस्वनः श्रवण - कर्षि - सच्छिञ्जितः सनर्म - रस - सूचकाक्षर - पदार्थ - भङ्ग्युक्तिकः ।
रमादिक - वराङ्गना - हृदय - हारि - वंशी - कलः स मे मदन - मोहनः सखि तनोति कर्ण - स्पृहाम् ॥40॥
cc-antya-17.40.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "My dear friend, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, has a voice as deep as a cloud resounding in the sky. With the tinkling of His ornaments, He attracts the ears of the gopīs, and with the sound of His flute He attracts even the goddess of fortune and other beautiful women. That Personality of Godhead, known as Madana-mohana, whose joking words carry many indications and deep meanings, is increasing the lusty desires of My ears.'

lines: tāra eka śruti-kaṇe, ḍubāya jagatera kāṇe,
devanagari: “कण्ठेर गम्भीर ध्वनि, नवघन - ध्वनि जि नि’
यार गुणे कोकिल लाजाय ।
तार एक श्रुति - कणे, डुबाय जगतेर काणे
पुनः काण बाहुड़ि’ ना आय ॥41॥
cc-antya-17.41.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's deep voice is more resonant than newly arrived clouds, and His sweet song defeats even the sweet voice of the cuckoo. Indeed, His song is so sweet that even one particle of its sound can inundate the entire world. If such a particle enters one's ear, one is immediately bereft of all other types of hearing.

lines: kṛṣṇera se śabda-guṇe, harile āmāra kāṇe,
ebe nā pāya, tṛṣṇāya mari' yāya
devanagari: कह, सखि, कि करि उपाय ?
कृष्णेर से शब्द - गुणे, हरिले आमार काणे, ।
एबे ना पाय, तृष्णाय मरि’ याय ॥42॥
cc-antya-17.42.translation: "My dear friend, please tell me what to do. My ears have been plundered by the qualities of Kṛṣṇa's sound. Now, however, I cannot hear His transcendental sound, and I am almost dead for want of it.

lines: eka-bāra yei śune, vyāpi rahe' tāra kāṇe,
devanagari: नुपर - किङ्किणी - ध्वनि, हंस - सारस जि नि’
कङ्कण - ध्वनि चटके लाजाय ।
एक - बार येइ शुने, व्यापि रहे’ तार काणे
अन्य शब्द से - काणे ना याय ॥43॥
cc-antya-17.43.translation: "The tinkling of Kṛṣṇa's ankle bells surpasses the songs of even the swan and crane, and the sound of His bangles puts the singing of the caṭaka bird to shame. Having allowed these sounds to enter the ears even once, one cannot tolerate hearing anything else.

devanagari: से श्री - मुख - भाषित, अमृत हैते परामृत,
स्मित - कर्पूर ताहाते मिश्रित ।
शब्द, अर्थ, - दुइ - शक्ति, नाना - रस करे व्यक्ति ,
प्रत्यक्षर - नर्म - विभूषित ॥44॥
cc-antya-17.44.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's speech is far sweeter than nectar. Each of His jubilant words is full of meaning, and when His speech mixes with His smile, which is like camphor, the resultant sound and the deep meaning of Kṛṣṇa's words create various transcendental mellows.

lines: bhāgya-vaśe kabhu pāya, abhāgye kabhu nā pāya,
devanagari: से अमृतेर एक - कण, कर्ण - चकोर - जीवन
कर्ण - चकोर जीये सेइ आशे ।
भाग्य - वशे कभु पाय, अभाग्ये कभु ना पाय
ना पाइले मरये पियासे ॥45॥
cc-antya-17.45.translation: "One particle of that transcendental, blissful nectar is the life and soul of the ear, which is like a cakora bird that lives in hope of tasting that nectar. Sometimes, by good fortune, the bird can taste it, but at other times he unfortunately cannot and therefore almost dies of thirst.

lines: nīvi-bandha paḍe khasi', vinā-mūle haya dāsī,
devanagari: येबा वेणु - कल - ध्वनि, एक - बार ताहा शुनि’
जगन्नारी - चित्त आउलाय ।
नीवि - बन्ध पड़े ख सि’, विना - मूले हय दासी
बाउली ह ञा कृष्ण - पाशे धाय ॥46॥
cc-antya-17.46.translation: "The transcendental vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute disturbs the hearts of women all over the world, even if they hear it only once. Thus their fastened belts become loose, and these women become the unpaid maidservants of Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, they run toward Kṛṣṇa exactly like madwomen.

lines: yebā lakṣmī-ṭhākurāṇī, teṅho ye kākalī śuni',
nā pāya kṛṣṇera saṅga, bāḍe tṛṣṇā-taraṅga,
devanagari: येबा लक्ष्मी - ठाकुराणी, तेंहो ये काक ली शुनि’,
कृष्ण - पाश आइसे प्रत्याशाय ।
ना पाय कृष्णेर सङ्ग, बाड़े तृष्णा - तरङ्ग,
तप करे, तबु नाहि पाय ॥47॥
cc-antya-17.47.translation: "When she hears the vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute, even the goddess of fortune comes to Him, greatly hoping for His association, but nevertheless she does not get it. When the waves of thirst for His association increase, she performs austerities, but still she cannot meet Him.

lines: ei śabdāmṛta cāri, yāra haya bhāgya bhāri,
ihā yei nāhi śune, se kāṇa janmila kene,
devanagari: एइ शब्दामृत चारि, यार हय भाग्य भारि
सेइ कर्णे इहा करे पान ।
इहा येइ नाहि शुने, से काण जन्मिल केने
काणाकड़ि - सम सेइ काण” ॥48॥
cc-antya-17.48.translation: "Only the most fortunate can hear these four nectarean sounds-Kṛṣṇa's words, the tinkling of His ankle bells and bangles, His voice and the vibration of His flute. If one does not hear these sounds, his ears are as useless as small conchshells with holes."

lines: karite aiche vilāpa, uṭhila udvega, bhāva,
udvega, viṣāda, mati, autsukya, trāsa, dhṛti, smṛti,
devanagari: करिते ऐछे विलाप, उठिल उद्वेग, भाव,
मने काहो नाहि आलम्बन ।
उद्वेग, विषाद, मति, औत्सुक्य, त्रास, धृति, स्मृति,
नाना - भावेर ह - इल मिलन ॥49॥
cc-antya-17.49.translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented in this way, agitation and ecstasy awoke in His mind, and He became very restless. Many transcendental ecstasies combined in Him, including anxiety, lamentation, attention, eagerness, fear, determination and remembrance.

lines: yabe yei bhāva prabhura karaye udaya
devanagari: यबे येइ भाव प्रभुर करये उदय ।
भावानुरूप गीत गाय स्वरूप - महाशय ॥5॥
cc-antya-17.5.translation: As they talked of Kṛṣṇa, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī would sing songs exactly suitable for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's transcendental emotions.

lines: bhāva-śābalye rādhāra ukti, līlā-śuke haila sphūrti,
unmādera sāmarthye, sei ślokera kare arthe,
devanagari: भाव - शाबल्ये राधार उक्ति, लीला - शुके हैल स्फूर्ति
सेइ भावे पड़े एक श्लोक ।
उन्मादेर सामर्थ्य, सेइ श्लोकेर करे अर्थे
येइ अर्थ नाहि जाने लोक ॥50॥
cc-antya-17.50.translation: The aggregate of all these ecstasies awoke a statement by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in the mind of Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura [Līlā-śuka]. In the same ecstatic mood, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu now recited that verse, and on the strength of madness, He described its meaning, which is unknown to people in general.

lines: kim iha kṛṇumaḥ kasya brūmaḥ kṛtaṁ kṛtam āśayā
kathayata kathām anyāṁ dhanyām aho hṛdaye śayaḥ
kṛpaṇa-kṛpaṇā kṛṣṇe tṛṣṇā ciraṁ bata lambate
devanagari: किमिह कृणुमः कस्य ब्रूमः कृतं कृतमाशया कथयत कथामन्यां धन्यामहो हृदये शयः ।
मधुर - मधुर - स्मेराकारे मनोनयनोत्सवे कृपण - कृपणा कृष्णे तृष्णा चिरं बत लम्बते ॥51॥
cc-antya-17.51.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'Alas, what shall I do? To whom shall I speak? Let whatever I have done in hopes of meeting Kṛṣṇa be finished now. Please say something auspicious, but do not speak about Kṛṣṇa. Alas, Kṛṣṇa is lying within My heart like Cupid; therefore how can I possibly give up talking of Him? I cannot forget Kṛṣṇa, whose smile is sweeter than sweetness itself and who gives pleasure to My mind and eyes. Alas, My great thirst for Kṛṣṇa is increasing moment by moment!'

lines: "ei kṛṣṇera virahe, udvege mana sthira nahe,
yebā tumi sakhī-gaṇa, viṣāde bāula mana,
devanagari: “एइ कृष्णेर विरहे, उद्वेगे मन स्थिर नहे ,
प्राप्त्युपाय - चिन्तन ना याय ।
येबा तुमि सखी - गण, विषादे बाउल मन ,
कारे पुछों, के कहे उपाय ? ॥52॥
cc-antya-17.52.translation: "The anxiety caused by separation from Kṛṣṇa has made Me impatient, and I can think of no way to meet Him. O My friends, you are also deranged by lamentation. Who, therefore, will tell Me how to find Him?

lines: hā hā sakhi, ki kari upāya!
kāṅhā karoṅ, kāhāṅ yāṅa, kāhāṅ gele kṛṣṇa pāṅa,
devanagari: हा हा सखि, कि करि उपाय!
काँहा करों, काहाँ याङ, काहाँ गेले कृष्ण पाङ ।
कृष्ण विना प्राण मोर याय” ॥53॥
cc-antya-17.53.translation: "O My dear friends, how shall I find Kṛṣṇa? What shall I do? Where shall I go? Where can I meet Him? Because I cannot find Kṛṣṇa, My life is leaving Me."

lines: kṣaṇe mana sthira haya, tabe mane vicāraya,
devanagari: क्षणे मन स्थिर हय, तबे मने विचारय
बलिते ह - इल भावोद्गम ।
पिङ्गलार वचन - स्मृति, कराइल भाव - मति
ताते करे अर्थ - निर्धारण ॥54॥
cc-antya-17.54.translation: Suddenly, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became calm and considered His state of mind. He remembered the words of Piṅgalā, and this aroused an ecstasy that moved Him to speak. Thus He explained the meaning of the verse.

lines: chāḍa' kṛṣṇa-kathā adhanya, kaha anya-kathā dhanya,
devanagari: “देखि एइ उपाये, कृष्ण - आशा छा ड़ि’ दिये
आशा छाड़िले सुखी हय मन ।
छाड़’ कृष्ण - कथा अधन्य, कह अन्य - कथा धन्य
याते हय कृष्ण - विस्मरण” ॥55॥
cc-antya-17.55.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'If I give up hope of meeting Kṛṣṇa, I shall then be happy. Therefore, let us stop this most inglorious discussion of Kṛṣṇa. It would be better for us to talk of glorious topics and forget Him.'

lines: kahitei ha-ila smṛti, citte haila kṛṣṇa-sphūrti,
"yāre cāhi chāḍite, sei śuñā āche citte,
devanagari: कहितेइ ह - इल स्मृति, चित्ते हैल कृष्ण - स्फूर्ति
सखीरे कहे ह ञा विस्मिते ।
यारे चाहि छाड़िते, सेइ शुञा आछे चित्ते
कोन रीते ना पारि छाड़िते” ॥56॥
cc-antya-17.56.translation: "While speaking in this way, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī suddenly remembered Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, He appeared within Her heart. Greatly astonished, She told Her friends, 'The person I want to forget is lying in My heart.'

lines: kahe—"ye jagat māre, se paśila antare,
devanagari: राधा - भावेर स्वभाव आन, कृष्णे कराय’काम’ - ज्ञान
काम - ज्ञाने त्रास हैल चित्ते ।
कहे - “ये जगत्मारे, से पशिल अन्तरे
एइ वैरी ना देय पासरिते” ॥57॥
cc-antya-17.57.translation: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's ecstasy also made Her think of Kṛṣṇa as Cupid, and this understanding frightened Her. She said, 'This Cupid, who has conquered the whole world and entered My heart, is My greatest enemy, for He does not allow Me to forget Him.'

lines: mane ha-ila lālasa, nā haya āpana-vaśa,
devanagari: औत्सुक्येर प्रावीण्ये, जिति’ अन्य भाव - सैन्ये,
उदय हैल निज - राज्य - मने ।
मने ह - इल लालस, ना हय आपन - वश,
दुःखे मने करेन भर्सने ॥58॥
cc-antya-17.58.translation: "Then great eagerness conquered all the other soldiers of ecstasy, and an uncontrollable desire arose in the kingdom of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's mind. Greatly unhappy, She then chastised Her own mind.

lines: "mana mora vāma-dīna, jala vinā yena mīna,
devanagari: “मन मोर वाम - दीन, जल विना येन मीन
कृष्ण विना क्षणे मरि’ याय ।
मधुर - हास्य - वदने, मन - नेत्र - रसायने
कृष्ण - तृष्णा द्विगुण बाड़ाय ॥59॥
cc-antya-17.59.translation: “ 'If I do not think of Kṛṣṇa, My impoverished mind will die within a moment like a fish out of water. But when I see Kṛṣṇa's sweetly smiling face, My mind and eyes are so pleased that My desire for Him redoubles.

devanagari: विद्यापति, चण्डीदास, श्री - गीत - गोविन्द ।
भावानुरूप श्लोक पड़ेन राय - रामानन्द ॥6॥
cc-antya-17.6.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya would quote verses from the books of Vidyāpati and Caṇḍīdāsa, and especially from the Gīta-govinda by Jayadeva Gosvāmī, to complement the ecstasy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

lines: hā hā kṛṣṇa prāṇa-dhana, hā hā padma-locana,
hā hā śyāma-sundara, hā hā pītāmbara-dhara,
devanagari: हा हा कृष्ण प्राण - धन, हा हा पद्म - लोचन
हा हा दिव्य सद्गुण - सागर! ।
हा हा श्याम सुन्दर, हा हा पीताम्बर - धर
हा हा रास - विलास नागर ॥60॥
cc-antya-17.60.translation: “ 'Alas! Where is Kṛṣṇa, the treasure of My life? Where is the lotus-eyed one? Alas! Where is the divine ocean of all transcendental qualities? Alas! Where is the beautiful, blackish youth dressed in yellow garments? Alas! Where is the hero of the rāsa dance?

lines: kāhāṅ gele tomā pāi, tumi kaha,—tāhāṅ yāi",
svarūpa uṭhi' kole kari', prabhure ānila dhari',
devanagari: काहाँ गेले तोमा पाइ, तुमि कह, - ताहाँ याइ”,
एत कहि’ चलिला धा ञा ।
स्वरूप उठि’ कोले करि’, प्रभुरे आनिल धरि’,
निज - स्थाने वसाइला लै ञा ॥61॥
cc-antya-17.61.translation: “ 'Where shall I go? Where can I find You? Please tell Me. I shall go there.' " Speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began running. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, however, stood up, caught Him and took Him on his lap. Then Svarūpa Dāmodara brought Him back to His place and made Him sit down.

lines: kṣaṇeke prabhura bāhya haila, svarūpere ājñā dila,
devanagari: क्षणेके प्रभुर बाह्य हैल, स्वरूपेरे आज्ञा दिल ,
“स्वरूप, किछु कर मधुर गान” ।
स्वरूप गाय विद्यापति, गीत - गोविन्द - गीति,
शुनि’ प्रभुर जुड़ाइल काण ॥62॥
cc-antya-17.62.translation: Suddenly Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to external consciousness and said to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, "My dear Svarūpa, please sing some sweet songs." The Lord's ears were satisfied when He heard Svarūpa Dāmodara sing songs from Gīta-govinda and those by the poet Vidyāpati.

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु प्रति - रात्रि - दिने ।
उन्माद चेष्टित हय प्रलाप - वचने ॥63॥
cc-antya-17.63.translation: Each day and night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would become deranged in this way and talk like a madman.

lines: sahasra-mukhe varṇe yadi, nāhi pāya pāra
devanagari: एक - दिने यत हय भावेर विकार ।
सहस्त्र - मुखे वर्णे यदि, नाहि पाय पार ॥64॥
cc-antya-17.64.translation: Even Anantadeva, who possesses thousands of mouths, cannot fully describe the ecstatic transformations that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu experienced in a single day.

lines: jīva dīna ki karibe tāhāra varṇana?
devanagari: जीव दीन कि करिबे ताहार वर्णन ? ।
शाखा - चन्द्र - न्याय क रि’ दिग्दरशन ॥65॥
cc-antya-17.65.translation: What can a poor creature like me describe of those transformations? I can give only a hint of them, as if showing the moon through the branches of a tree.

lines: ihā yei śune, tāra juḍāya mana-kāṇa
devanagari: इहा येइ शुने, तार जुड़ाय मन - काण ।
अलौकिक गूढ़ - प्रेम - चेष्टा हय ज्ञान ॥66॥
cc-antya-17.66.translation: This description, however, will satisfy the mind and ears of anyone who hears it, and he will be able to understand these uncommon activities of deep ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: अद्भुत निगूढ़ प्रेमेर माधुर्य - महिमा ।
आपनि आस्वादि’ प्रभु देखाइला सीमा ॥67॥
cc-antya-17.67.translation: Ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa is wonderfully deep. By personally tasting the glorious sweetness of that love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed us its extreme limit.

lines: aiche dayālu dātā loke nāhi śuni anya
devanagari: अद्भुत - दयालु चैतन्य - अद्भुत - वदान्य! ।
ऐछे दयालु दाता लोके नाहि शुनि अन्य ॥68॥
cc-antya-17.68.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is wonderfully merciful and wonderfully magnanimous. We have heard of no one else within this world so merciful and charitable.

devanagari: सर्व - भावे भज, लोक, चैतन्य - चरण ।
याहा हैते पाइबा कृष्ण - प्रेमामृत - धन ॥69॥
cc-antya-17.69.translation: Worship the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in all respects. Only in this way will you achieve the nectarean treasure of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

lines: madhye madhye āpane prabhu śloka paḍiyā
ślokera artha karena prabhu vilāpa kariyā
devanagari: मध्ये मध्ये आपने प्रभु श्लोक पड़िया ।
श्लोकेर अर्थ करेन प्रभु विलाप करिया ॥7॥
cc-antya-17.7.translation: At intervals, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would also recite a verse. Then, in great lamentation, He would explain it.

devanagari: एइ त’ कहिलुँ ‘कूर्माकृति’ - अनुभाव ।
उन्माद - चेष्टित ताते उन्माद - प्रलाप ॥70॥
cc-antya-17.70.translation: Thus I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's ecstatic transformation of becoming like a tortoise. In that ecstasy, He talked and acted like a madman.

devanagari: एइ लीला स्व - ग्रन्थे रघुनाथ - दास ।
गौराङ्ग - स्तव - कल्पवृक्षे कैराछेन प्रकाश ॥71॥
cc-antya-17.71.translation: Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī has fully described this pastime in his book Gaurāṅga-stava-kalpavṛkṣa.
