lines: anudghāṭya dvāra-trayam uru ca bhitti-trayam aho
virājan gaurāṅgo hṛdaya udayan māṁ madayati
devanagari: अनुद्धाट्य द्वार - त्रयमुरु च भित्ति - त्रयमहो विलछ्योच्चैः कालिङ्गिक - सुरभि - मध्ये निपतितः ।
तनूद्यत्सङ्कोचात्कमठ इव कृष्णोरु - विरहाद् विराज न्गौराङ्गो हृदय उदयन्मां मदयति ॥72॥
cc-antya-17.72.translation: "How wonderful it is! Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left His residence without opening the three strongly bolted doors. Then He crossed over three high walls, and later, because of strong feelings of separation from Kṛṣṇa, He fell down amidst the cows of the Tailaṅga district and retracted all the limbs of His body like a tortoise. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who appeared in that way, rises in my heart and maddens me."

devanagari: श्री - रूप - रघुनाथ - पदे यार आश ।
चैतन्य - चरितामृत कहे कृष्णदास ॥73॥
cc-antya-17.73.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

lines: gosāñire śayana karāi' duṅhe ghare gela
devanagari: एइ - मते नाना - भावे अर्ध - रात्रि हैल ।
गोसाञि रे शयन करा इ’ दुँहे घरे गेल ॥8॥
cc-antya-17.8.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed half the night experiencing varieties of emotions. Finally, after making the Lord lie down on His bed, both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya returned to their homes.

devanagari: गम्भीरार द्वारे गोविन्द करिला शयन ।
सब - रात्रि प्रभु करेन उच्च - सङ्कीर्तन ॥9॥
cc-antya-17.9.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal servant, Govinda, lay down at the door of His room, and the Lord very loudly chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra all night.

lines: nimagno mūrcchālaḥ payasi nivasan rātrim akhilāṁ
prabhāte prāptaḥ svair avatu sa śacī-sūnur iha naḥ
devanagari: शरज्ज्यो त्स्ना - सिन्धोरवकलनया जात - यमुना - भ्रमाद्धावन् योऽस्मिन्हरि - विरह - तापार्ण व इव ।
निमग्नो मूर्च्छालः पयसि निवसध्रात्रिमखि लां प्रभाते प्राप्तः स्वैरवतु स शची - सूनुरिह नः ॥1॥
cc-antya-18.1.translation: In the brilliant autumn moonlight, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mistook the sea for the River Yamunā. Greatly afflicted by separation from Kṛṣṇa, He ran and dove into the sea and remained unconscious in the water the entire night. In the morning, He was found by His personal devotees. May that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, protect us by His transcendental pastimes.

lines: se saba ślokera artha, se saba 'vikāra'
se saba varṇite grantha haya ati-vistāra
devanagari: से सब श्लोकेर अर्थ, से सब ‘विकार’ ।
से सब वर्णिते ग्रन्थ हय अति - विस्तार ॥10॥
cc-antya-18.10.translation: To explain fully all those verses and all the transformations that took place in the Lord's body would require a very large volume.

lines: aiche vicitra krīḍā kari', tīre āilā śrī-hari,
devanagari: ऐछे विचित्र क्रीड़ा क रि’, तीरे आइला श्री - हरि
सङ्गे लञा सब कान्ता - गण ।
गन्ध - तैल - मर्दन, आमलकी - उद्वर्तन
सेवा करे ती रे सखी - गण ॥100॥
cc-antya-18.100.translation: "After performing such wonderful pastimes, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa got up on the shore of the Yamunā River, taking with Him all His beloved gopīs. Then the gopīs on the riverbank rendered service by massaging Kṛṣṇa and the other gopīs with scented oil and smearing paste of āmalakī fruit on their bodies.

devanagari: पुनरपि कैल स्नान, शुष्क - वस्त्र परिधान
रत्न - मन्दिरे कैला आगमन ।
वृन्दा - कृत सम्भार, गन्ध - पुष्प - अलङ्कार
वन्य - वेश करिल रचन ॥101॥
cc-antya-18.101.translation: "Then they all bathed again, and after putting on dry clothing, they went to a small jeweled house, where the gopī Vṛndā arranged to dress them in forest clothing by decorating them with fragrant flowers, green leaves and all kinds of other ornaments.

devanagari: वृन्दावने तरु - लता, अद्भुत ताहार कथा
बार - मास धरे फुल - फल ।
वृन्दावने देवी - गण, कुञ्ज - दासी यत जन
फल पा ड़ि’ आनिया सकल ॥102॥
cc-antya-18.102.translation: "In Vṛndāvana, the trees and creepers are wonderful because throughout the entire year they produce all kinds of fruits and flowers. The gopīs and maidservants in the bowers of Vṛndāvana pick these fruits and flowers and bring them before Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

lines: uttama saṁskāra kari', baḍa baḍa thālī bhari',
bhakṣaṇera krama kari', dhariyāche sāri sāri,
devanagari: उत्तम संस्कार करि’, बड़ बड़ थाली भ रि’
रत्न - मन्दिरे पिण्डार उपरे ।
भक्षणेर क्रम क रि’, धरियाछे सारि सारि
आगे आसन वसिबार तरे ॥103॥
cc-antya-18.103.translation: "The gopīs peeled all the fruits and placed them together on large plates on a platform in the jeweled cottage. They arranged the fruit in orderly rows for eating, and in front of it they made a place to sit.

lines: eka nārikela nānā-jāti, eka āmra nānā bhāti,
panasa, kharjura, kamalā, nāraṅga, jāma, santarā,
devanagari: एक नारिकेल नाना - जाति, एक आम्र नाना भाति ,
कला, कोलि - विविध - प्रकार ।
पनस, खर्जुर, कमला, नारङ्ग, जाम, सन्तरा ,
द्राक्षा, बादाम, मेओया यत आर ॥104॥
cc-antya-18.104.translation: "Among the fruits were many varieties of coconut and mango, bananas, berries, jackfruits, dates, tangerines, oranges, blackberries, santarās, grapes, almonds and all kinds of dried fruit.

lines: kharamujā, kṣīrikā, tāla, keśura, pānī-phala, mṛṇāla,
kona deśe kāra khyāti, vṛndāvane saba-prāpti,
devanagari: खरमुजा, क्षीरिका, ताल, केशुर, पानी - फल, मृणाल,
बिल्व, पीलु, दाड़िम्बादि यत ।
कोन देशे कार ख्याति, वृन्दावने सब - प्राप्ति,
सहस्र - जाति, लेखा याय कत ? ॥105॥
cc-antya-18.105.translation: "There were cantaloupes, kṣirikās, palmfruits, keśuras, waterfruits, lotus fruits, bel, pīlu, pomegranate and many others. Some of them are variously known in different places, but in Vṛndāvana they are always available in so many thousands of varieties that no one can fully describe them.

devanagari: गङ्गाजल, अमृतकेलि, पीयूषग्रन्थि, कर्पूरकेलि,
सरपूरी, अमृति, पद्मचिनि ।
खण्ड - क्षीरसार - वृक्ष, घरे क रि’ नाना भक्ष्य ,
राधा याहा कृष्ण लागि’ आनि ॥106॥
cc-antya-18.106.translation: "At home Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī had made various types of sweetmeats from milk and sugar, such as gaṅgājala, amṛtakeli, pīyūṣagranthi, karpūrakeli, sarapūrī, amṛti, padmacini and khaṇḍa-kṣīrisāra-vṛkṣa. She had then brought them all for Kṛṣṇa.

lines: bhakṣyera paripāṭī dekhi', kṛṣṇa hailā mahā-sukhī,
saṅge lañā sakhī-gaṇa, rādhā kailā bhojana,
devanagari: भक्ष्येर परिपाटी दे खि’, कृष्ण हैला महा - सुखी
वसि’ कैल वन्य भोजन ।
सङ्गे लञा सखी - गण, राधा कैला भोजन
दुँहे कैला मन्दिरे शयन ॥107॥
cc-antya-18.107.translation: "When Kṛṣṇa saw the very nice arrangement of food, He happily sat down and had a forest picnic. Then, after Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her gopī friends partook of the remnants, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa lay down together in the jeweled house.

lines: rādhā-kṛṣṇa nidrā gelā, sakhī-gaṇa śayana kailā,
devanagari: केह करे वीजन, केह पाद - सम्वाहन
केह कराय ताम्बूल भक्षण ।
राधा - कृष्ण निद्रा गेला, सखी - गण शयन कैला
देखि’ आमार सुखी हैल मन ॥108॥
cc-antya-18.108.translation: "Some of the gopīs fanned Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, others massaged Their feet, and some fed Them betel leaves to chew. When Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa fell asleep, all the other gopīs also lay down. When I saw this, My mind was very happy.

lines: kāṅhā yamunā, vṛndāvana, kāṅhā kṛṣṇa, gopī-gaṇa,
devanagari: हेन - काले मोरे धरि, महा - कोलाहल क रि’,
तुमि - सब इहाँ लञा आइला ।
काँहा यमुना, वृन्दावन, काँहा कृष्ण, गोपी - गण,
सेइ सुख भङ्ग कराइला!” ॥109॥
cc-antya-18.109.translation: "Suddenly, all of you created a great tumult and picked Me up and brought Me back here. Where now is the River Yamunā? Where is Vṛndāvana? Where are Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs? You have broken My happy dream!"

lines: dvādaśa vatsare ye ye līlā kṣaṇe-kṣaṇe
devanagari: द्वादश व त्सरे ये ये लीला क्षण - क्षणे ।
अति - बाहुल्य - भये ग्रन्थ ना कैलुँ लिखने ॥11॥
cc-antya-18.11.translation: So as not to increase the size of this book, I have not written about all the Lord's pastimes, for He performed them every moment of every day for twelve years.

devanagari: एतेक कहिते प्रभुर केवल ‘बाह्य’ हैल ।
स्वरूप - गोसाञि रे देखि’ ताँहारे पुछिल ॥110॥
cc-antya-18.110.translation: Speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fully returned to external consciousness. Seeing Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, the Lord questioned him.

devanagari: ‘इहाँ केने तोमरा आमारे लञा आइला ?’ ।
स्वरूप - गोसाञि तबे कहिले लागिला ॥111॥
cc-antya-18.111.translation: "Why have you brought Me here?" He asked. Then Svarūpa Dāmodara answered Him.

lines: samudreṛa taraṅge āsi, eta dūra āilā!
devanagari: “यमुनार भ्रमे तुमि समुद्रे पड़िला ।
समुद्रेर तरङ्गे आसि, एत दूर आइला! ॥112॥
cc-antya-18.112.translation: "You mistook the sea for the Yamunā River," he said, "and You jumped into it. You have been carried this far by the waves of the sea.

lines: ei jāliyā jāle kari' tomā uṭhāila
tomāra paraśe ei preme matta ha-ila
devanagari: एइ जालिया जाले क रि’ तोमा उठाइल ।
तोमार परशे एइ प्रेमे मत्त ह - इल ॥113॥
cc-antya-18.113.translation: "This fisherman caught You in his net and rescued You from the water. Because of Your touch, he is now mad with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

lines: saba rātri sabe beḍāi tomāre anveṣiyā
devanagari: सब रात्रि सबे बेड़ाइ तोमारे अन्वेषि या ।
जालियार मुखे शुनि’ पाइनु आसिया ॥114॥
cc-antya-18.114.translation: "Throughout the night, we all walked about in search of You. After hearing from this fisherman, we came here and found You.

lines: tomāra mūrcchā dekhi' sabe mane pāi pīḍā
devanagari: तुमि मूर्च्छा - छले वृन्दावने देख क्रीड़ा ।
तोमार मूर्च्छा देखि’ सबे मने पाइ पीड़ा ॥115॥
cc-antya-18.115.translation: "While apparently unconscious, You witnessed the pastimes in Vṛndāvana, but when we saw You unconscious, we suffered great agony in our minds.

lines: tāte ye pralāpa kailā, tāhā ye śunila"
devanagari: कृष्ण - नाम ल - इते तोमार ‘अर्ध - बाह्य’ ह - इल ।
ताते ये प्रलाप कैला, ताहा ये शुनिल” ॥116॥
cc-antya-18.116.translation: "When we chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, however, You came to semiconsciousness, and we have all been hearing You speak like a madman."

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - “स्वप्ने दे खि’ गेलाङवृन्दावने ।
देखि, - कृष्ण रास करेन गोपीगण - सने ॥117॥
cc-antya-18.117.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "In My dream I went to Vṛndāvana, where I saw Lord Kṛṣṇa perform the rāsa dance with all the gopīs.

lines: dekhi' āmi pralāpa kailuṅ—hena laya mane"
devanagari: जल - क्रीडा क रि’ कैला वन्य - भोजने ।
देखि’ आमि प्रलाप कैलुँ - हेन लय मने” ॥118॥
cc-antya-18.118.translation: "After sporting in the water, Kṛṣṇa enjoyed a picnic. I can understand that after seeing this, I must certainly have talked like a madman."

lines: prabhure lañā ghara āilā ānandita hañā
devanagari: तबे स्वरूप - गोसाञि ताँरे स्नान करा ञा ।
प्रभुरे लञा घर आइला आनन्दित ह ञा ॥119॥
cc-antya-18.119.translation: Thereafter, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī had Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathe in the sea, and then he very happily brought Him back home.

devanagari: पूर्वे येइ देखाञाछि दिग्दरशन ।
तैछे जानिह ‘विकार’ ‘प्रलाप’ वर्णन ॥12॥
cc-antya-18.12.translation: As I have previously indicated, I am describing the mad speeches and bodily transformations of the Lord only in brief.

devanagari: एइ त कहिलुँ प्रभुर समुद्र - पतन ।
इहा येइ शुने, पाय चैतन्य - चरण ॥120॥
cc-antya-18.120.translation: Thus I have described the incident of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's falling into the ocean. Anyone who listens to this pastime will certainly attain shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: श्री - रूप - रघुनाथ - पदे यार आश ।
चैतन्य - चरितामृत कहे कृष्णदास ॥121॥
cc-antya-18.121.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

lines: eka-dinera līlāra tabu nāhi pāya anta
devanagari: सहस्र - वदने यबे कहये ‘अनन्त’ ।
एक - दिनेर लीलार तबु नाहि पाय अन्त ॥13॥
cc-antya-18.13.translation: If Ananta, with His one thousand hoods, tried to describe even one day's pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He would find them impossible to describe fully.

lines: eka-dinera līlāra tabu nāhi pāya śeṣa
devanagari: कोटि - युग पर्यन्त यदि लिखये गणेश ।
एक - दिनेर लीलार तबु नाहि पाय शेष ॥14॥
cc-antya-18.14.translation: If Gaṇeśa, Lord Śiva's son and the expert scribe of the demigods, tried for millions of millenniums to fully describe one day of the Lord's pastimes, he would be unable to find their limit.

lines: kṛṣṇa yāra nā pāya anta, kebā chāra āra?
devanagari: भक्तेर प्रेम - विकार दे खि’ कृष्णेर चमत्कार! ।
कृष्ण यार ना पाय अन्त, केबा छार आर ? ॥15॥
cc-antya-18.15.translation: Even Lord Kṛṣṇa is struck with wonder at seeing the transformations of ecstasy in His devotees. If Kṛṣṇa Himself cannot estimate the limits of such emotions, how could others?

lines: bhakta-premāra yata daśā, ye gati prakāra
yata duḥkha, yata sukha, yateka vikāra
devanagari: भक्त - प्रेमार यत दशा, ये गति प्रकार ।
यत दुःख, यत सुख, यतेक विकार ॥16॥
cc-antya-18.16-17.translation: Kṛṣṇa Himself cannot fully understand the conditions, the mode of progress, the happiness and unhappiness, and the moods of ecstatic love of His devotees. He therefore accepts the role of a devotee to taste these emotions fully.

devanagari: कृष्णेरे नाचाय प्रेमा, भक्तेरे नाचाय ।
आपने नाचये , - तिने नाचे एक - ठाञि ॥18॥
cc-antya-18.18.translation: Ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa makes Kṛṣṇa and His devotees dance, and it also dances personally. In this way, all three dance together in one place.

lines: premāra vikāra varṇite cāhe yei jana
devanagari: प्रेमार विकार वर्णिते चाहे येइ जन ।
चान्द धरिते चाहे, येन हञा ‘वामन’ ॥19॥
cc-antya-18.19.translation: One who wants to describe the transformations of ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa is like a dwarf trying to catch the moon in the sky.

devanagari: जय जय श्री - चैतन्य जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैत - चन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-antya-18.2.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

devanagari: वायु यैछे सिन्धु - जलेर हरे एक ‘कण’ ।
कृष्ण - प्रेम - कण तैछे जीवेर स्पर्शन ॥20॥
cc-antya-18.20.translation: As the wind can carry away but a drop of the water in the ocean, a living entity can touch only a particle of the ocean of love of Kṛṣṇa.

lines: kṣaṇe kṣaṇe uṭhe premāra taraṅga ananta
jīva chāra kāhāṅ tāra pāibeka anta?
devanagari: क्षणे क्षणे उठे प्रेमार तरङ्ग अनन्त ।
जीव छार काहाँ तार पाइबेक अन्त ? ॥21॥
cc-antya-18.21.translation: Endless waves arise moment after moment in that ocean of love. How could an insignificant living entity estimate their limits?

devanagari: श्री - कृष्ण - चैतन्य याहा करेन आस्वादन ।
सबे एक जाने ताहा स्वरूपादिगण’ ॥22॥
cc-antya-18.22.translation: Only a person on the level of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī can fully know what Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tastes in His love for Kṛṣṇa.

lines: jīva hañā kare yei tāhāra varṇana
devanagari: जीव ह ञा करे येइ ताहार वर्णन ।
आपना शोधिते तार छोंये एक ‘कण’ ॥23॥
cc-antya-18.23.translation: When an ordinary living entity describes the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he purifies himself by touching one drop of that great ocean.

devanagari: एइ - मत रासेर श्लोक - सकल - इ पड़िला ।
शेषे जल - केलिर श्लोक पड़िते लागिला ॥24॥
cc-antya-18.24.translation: Thus all the verses about the rāsa-līlā dance were recited. Then finally the verse concerning the pastimes in the water was recited.

devanagari: ताभिर्युतः श्रममपोहितुमङ्ग - सङ्ग - घृष्ट - स्त्रजः स कुच - कुङ्कम - रञ्जितायाः ।
गन्धर्व - पालिभिरनुद्रुत आविशद्वाः श्रान्तो गजीभिरिभ - राङ् इव भिन्न - सेतुः ॥25॥
cc-antya-18.25.translation: "As an independent leader among elephants enters the water with its female elephants, Kṛṣṇa, who is transcendental to the Vedic principles of morality, entered the water of the Yamunā with the gopīs. His chest had brushed against their breasts, crushing His flower garland and coloring it with red kuṅkuma powder. Attracted by the fragrance of that garland, humming bumblebees followed Kṛṣṇa like celestial beings of Gandharvaloka. In this way, Lord Kṛṣṇa mitigated the fatigue of the rāsa dance."

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु भ्रमिते भ्रमिते ।
आइटोटा हैते समुद्र देखेन आचम्बिते ॥26॥
cc-antya-18.26.translation: While thus wandering near the temple of Āiṭoṭā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly saw the sea.

devanagari: चन्द्र - कान्त्ये उछलित तरङ्ग उज्वल ।
झलमल करे , - येन ‘यमुनार जल’ ॥27॥
cc-antya-18.27.translation: Brightened by the shining light of the moon, the high waves of the sea glittered like the waters of the River Yamunā.

devanagari: यमुनार भ्रमे प्रभु धाञा चलिला ।
अलक्षिते याइ’ सिन्धु - जले झाँप दिला ॥28॥
cc-antya-18.28.translation: Mistaking the sea for the Yamunā, the Lord ran swiftly and jumped into the water, unseen by the others.

lines: paḍitei haila mūrcchā, kichui nā jāne
kabhu ḍubāya, kabhu bhāsāya taraṅgera gaṇe
devanagari: पड़ितेइ हैल मूर्च्छा, किछुइ ना जाने ।
कभु डुबाय, कभु भासाय तरङ्गेर गणे ॥29॥
cc-antya-18.29.translation: Falling into the sea, He lost consciousness and could not understand where He was. Sometimes He sank beneath the waves, and sometimes He floated above them.

devanagari: एइ - मते महाप्रभु नीलाचले वैसे ।
रात्रि - दिने कृष्ण - विच्छेदार्णवे भासे ॥3॥
cc-antya-18.3.translation: While thus living at Jagannātha Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu floated all day and night in an ocean of separation from Kṛṣṇa.

lines: ke bujhite pāre ei caitanyera nāṭa?
devanagari: तरङ्गे वहिया फिरे, - येन शुष्क काष्ठ ।
के बुझिते पारे एइ चैतन्येर नाट? ॥30॥
cc-antya-18.30.translation: The waves carried Him here and there like a piece of dry wood. Who can understand this dramatic performance by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu?

lines: koṇārkera dike prabhure taraṅge lañā yāya
kabhu ḍubāñā rākhe, kabhu bhāsāñā lañā yāya
devanagari: कोणार्केर दिके प्रभुरे तरङ्गे लञा याय ।
कभु डुबाञा राखे, कभु भासाञा लञा याय ॥31॥
cc-antya-18.31.translation: Keeping the Lord sometimes submerged and sometimes afloat, the waves carried Him toward the Koṇārka temple.

devanagari: यमुनाते जल - केलि गोपी - गण - सङ्गे ।
कृष्ण करेन - महाप्रभु भग्न सेइ रङ्गे ॥32॥
cc-antya-18.32.translation: Lord Kṛṣṇa performed pastimes with the gopīs in the waters of the Yamunā, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fully merged in those pastimes.

devanagari: इहाँ स्वरूपादि - गण प्रभु ना देखिया ।
‘काहाँ गेला प्रभु?’ कहे चमकित ह ञा ॥33॥
cc-antya-18.33.translation: Meanwhile, all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara, lost sight of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Astonished, they began searching for Him, asking, "Where has the Lord gone?"

lines: prabhure nā dekhiyā saṁśaya karite lāgilā
devanagari: मनो - वेगे गेला प्रभु, देखिते नारिला ।
प्रभुरे ना देखिया संशय करिते लागिला ॥34॥
cc-antya-18.34.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had run off at the speed of mind. No one could see Him. Thus everyone was puzzled as to His whereabouts.

devanagari: ‘जगन्नाथ देखिते किबा देवालये गेला ? ।
अन्य उद्याने किबा उन्मादे पड़िला ? ॥35॥
cc-antya-18.35.translation: "Has the Lord gone to the temple of Jagannātha, or has He fallen down in madness in some garden?

devanagari: गुण्डिचा - मन्दिरे गेला, किबा नरेन्द्रेरे ?।
चटक - पर्वते गेला, किबा कोणाकर्ेरे ?’ ॥36॥
cc-antya-18.36.translation: "Perhaps He went to the Guṇḍicā temple, or to Lake Narendra, or to the Caṭaka-parvata. Maybe He went to the temple at Koṇārka."

lines: eta bali' sabe phire prabhure cāhiyā
samudrera tīre āilā kata jana lañā
devanagari: एत बलि’ सबे फिरे प्रभुरे चाहिया ।
समुद्रेर तीरे आइला कत जन लञा ॥37॥
cc-antya-18.37.translation: Talking like this, the devotees wandered here and there looking for the Lord. Finally they came to the shore, accompanied by many others.

devanagari: चाहिये बेड़ाइते ऐछे रात्रि - शेष हैल ।
‘अन्तर्धान ह - इला प्रभु’, - निश्चय करिल ॥38॥
cc-antya-18.38.translation: While they were searching for the Lord, the night ended, and thus they all decided, "Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has now disappeared."

lines: prabhura vicchede kāra dehe nāhi prāṇa
aniṣṭā-śaṅkā vinā kāra mane nāhi āna
devanagari: प्रभुर विच्छेदे कार देहे नाहि प्राण ।
अनिष्टा - शङ्का विना कार मने नाहि आन ॥39॥
cc-antya-18.39.translation: In separation from the Lord, everyone felt as though he had lost his very life. They concluded that there must have been some mishap. They could not think of anything else.

devanagari: शरत्कालेर रात्रि, सब चन्द्रिका - उज्वल ।
प्रभु निज - गण ल ञा बेड़ान रात्रि - सकल ॥4॥
cc-antya-18.4.translation: During a night of the autumn season when a full moon brightened everything, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered all night long with His devotees.

devanagari: “अनिष्ट - शङ्कीनि बन्धु - हृदयानि भवन्ति हि” ॥40॥
cc-antya-18.40.translation: "A relative or intimate friend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved."

devanagari: समुद्रेर तीरे आसि’ युकति करिला ।
चिरायु - पर्वत - दिके कत - जन गेला ॥41॥
cc-antya-18.41.translation: When they arrived at the seashore, they conferred among themselves. Then some of them sought out Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at Caṭaka-parvata.

lines: pūrva-diśāya cale svarūpa lañā kata jana
devanagari: पूर्व - दिशाय चले स्वरूप लञा कत जन ।
सिन्धु - तीरे - नीरे करेन प्रभुर अन्वेषण ॥42॥
cc-antya-18.42.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara proceeded east with others, looking for the Lord on the beach or in the water.

lines: tabu preme bule kari' prabhura anveṣaṇa
devanagari: विषादे विह्वल सबे, नाहिक ‘चेतन’ ।
तबु प्रेमे बुले करि’ प्रभुर अन्वेषण ॥43॥
cc-antya-18.43.translation: Everyone was overwhelmed with moroseness and almost unconscious, but out of ecstatic love they continued to wander here and there, searching for the Lord.

lines: dekhena—eka jāliyā āise kāndhe jāla kari'
devanagari: देखेन - एक जालिया आइसे कान्धे जाल क रि’ ।
cc-antya-18.44.translation: Passing along the beach, they saw a fisherman approaching with his net over his shoulder. Laughing, crying, dancing and singing, he kept repeating the holy name"Hari, Hari."

devanagari: जालियार चेष्टा दे खि’ सबार चमत्कार ।
स्वरूप - गोसाञि तारे पुछेन समाचार ॥45॥
cc-antya-18.45.translation: Seeing the activities of the fisherman, everyone was astonished. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, therefore, asked him for information.

devanagari: “कह, जालिया, एइ दिके देखिला एक - जन? ।
तोमार एइ दशा केने , - कहत’ कारण ?” ॥46॥
cc-antya-18.46.translation: "My dear fisherman," he said, "why are you behaving like this? Have you seen someone hereabouts? What is the cause of your behavior? Please tell us."

lines: jāliyā kahe,—"ihāṅ eka manuṣya nā dekhila
jāla vāhite eka mṛtaka mora jāle āila
devanagari: जालिया कहे , - “इहाँ एक मनुष्य ना देखिल ।
जाल वाहिते एक मृतक मोर जाले आइल ॥47॥
cc-antya-18.47.translation: The fisherman replied, "I have not seen a single person here, but while casting my net in the water, I captured a dead body.

lines: baḍa matsya bali' āmi uṭhāiluṅ yatane
mṛtaka dekhite mora bhaya haila mane
devanagari: बड़ मत्स्य बलि’ आमि उठाइलें यतने ।
मृतक देखिते मोर भय हैल मने ॥48॥
cc-antya-18.48.translation: "I lifted it with great care, thinking it a big fish, but as soon as I saw that it was a corpse, great fear arose in my mind.

devanagari: जाल खसाइते तार अङ्ग - स्पर्श ह - इल ।
स्पर्श - मात्रे सेइ भूत हृदये पशिल ॥49॥
cc-antya-18.49.translation: "As I tried to release the net, I touched the body, and as soon as I touched it, a ghost entered my heart.

devanagari: उद्याने उद्याने भ्रमेन कौतुक देखिते ।
रास - लीलार गीत - श्लोक पड़िते शुनिते ॥5॥
cc-antya-18.5.translation: He walked from garden to garden, seeing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa and hearing and reciting songs and verses concerning the rāsa-līlā.

lines: bhaye kampa haila, mora netre vahe jala
devanagari: भये कम्प हैल, मोर नेत्रे वहे जल ।
गद्गद वाणी, रोम उठिल सकल ॥50॥
cc-antya-18.50.translation: "I shivered in fear and shed tears. My voice faltered, and all the hairs on my body stood up.

lines: kibā brahma-daitya, kibā bhūta, kahane nā yāya
devanagari: किबा ब्रह्म - दैत्य, किबा भूत, कहने ना याय ।
दर्शन - मात्रे मनुष्येर पैशे सेइ काय ॥51॥
cc-antya-18.51.translation: "I do not know whether it was the ghost of a dead brāhmaṇa or an ordinary man, but as soon as one looks upon it, it enters his body.

devanagari: शरीर दीघल तार - हात पाँच - सात ।
एकेक - हस्त - पद तार, तिन तिन हात ॥52॥
cc-antya-18.52.translation: "The body of this ghost is very long, five to seven cubits. Each of its arms and legs is as much as three cubits long.

lines: tāhā dekhi' prāṇa kā'ra nāhi rahe dhaḍe
devanagari: अस्थि - सन्धि छुटिले चर्म करे नड़ - बड़े ।
ताहा दे खि’ प्राण कार नाहि रहे धड़े ॥53॥
cc-antya-18.53.translation: "Its joints are all separated beneath the skin, which is completely slack. No one could see it and remain alive in his body.

lines: kabhu goṅ-goṅ kare, kabhu rahe acetana
devanagari: मड़ा - रूप ध रि’ रहे उत्तान - नयन ।
कभु गों - गों करे, कभु रहे अचेतन ॥54॥
cc-antya-18.54.translation: "That ghost has taken the form of a corpse, but he keeps his eyes open. Sometimes he utters the sounds'goṅ-goṅ,' and sometimes he remains unconscious.

lines: mui maile mora kaiche jīve strī-put
devanagari: साक्षात् देखेछों, - मोरे पाइल सेइ भूत ।
मुइ मैले मोर कैछे जीवे स्त्री - पुत् ॥55॥
cc-antya-18.55.translation: "I have seen that ghost directly, and he is haunting me. But if I die, who will take care of my wife and children?

lines: sei ta' bhūtera kathā kahana nā yāya
devanagari: सेइ त’ भूतेर कथा कहन ना याय ।
ओझा - ठाञि याइछों, - यदि से भूत छाड़ाय ॥56॥
cc-antya-18.56.translation: "The ghost is certainly very difficult to talk about, but I am going to find an exorcist and ask him if he can release me from it.

lines: ekā rātrye buli' matsya māriye nirjane
devanagari: एका रात्र्ये बुलि’ मत्स्य मारिये निर्जने ।
भूत - प्रेत आमार ना लागे ‘नृसिंह’ - स्मरणे ॥57॥
cc-antya-18.57.translation: "I wander alone at night killing fish in solitary places, but because I remember the hymn to Lord Nṛsiṁha, ghosts do not touch me.

lines: tāhāra ākāra dekhite bhaya lāge mane
devanagari: एइ भूत नृसिंह - नामे चापये द्विगुणे ।
ताहार आकार देखिते भय लागे मने ॥58॥
cc-antya-18.58.translation: "This ghost, however, overcomes me with redoubled strength when I chant the Nṛsiṁha mantra. When I even see the form of this ghost, great fear arises in my mind.

lines: othā nā yāiha, āmi niṣedhi tomāre
tāhāṅ gele sei bhūta lāgibe sabāre"
devanagari: ओथा ‘ना याइह, आमि निषेधि तोमारे ।
ताहाँ गेले सेइ भूत लागिबे सबारे” ॥59॥
cc-antya-18.59.translation: "Do not go near there. I forbid you. If you go, that ghost will catch you all."

devanagari: प्रभु प्रेमावेशे करेन गान, नर्तन ।
कभु भावावेशे रास - लीलानुकरण ॥6॥
cc-antya-18.6.translation: He sang and danced in ecstatic love and sometimes imitated the rāsa dance in emotional ecstasy.

lines: eta śuni' svarūpa-gosāñi saba tattva jāni'
devanagari: एत शुनि’ स्वरूप - गोसाञि सब तत्त्व जा नि’ ।
जालियारे किछु कय सुमधुर वाणी ॥60॥
cc-antya-18.60.translation: Hearing this, Svarūpa Dāmodara could understand the full truth of the matter. He spoke sweetly to the fisherman.

lines: mantra paḍi' śrī-hasta dilā tāhāra māthāte
devanagari: ‘आमि - बड़ ओझा जानि भूत छाड़ाइते’ ।
मन्त्र प ड़ि’ श्री - हस्त दिला ताहार माथाते ॥61॥
cc-antya-18.61.translation: "I am a famous exorcist," he said, "and I know how to rid you of this ghost." He then chanted some mantras and placed his hand on the top of the fisherman's head.

devanagari: तिन चापड़ मा रि’ कहे, - ‘भूत पलाइल ।
भय ना पाइह ‘ - बलि’ सुस्थिर करिल ॥62॥
cc-antya-18.62.translation: He slapped the fisherman three times and said, "Now the ghost has gone away. Do not be afraid." By saying this, he pacified the fisherman.

devanagari: एके प्रेम, आरे भय , - द्विगुण अस्थिर ।
भय - अंश गेल, - से हैल किछु धीर ॥63॥
cc-antya-18.63.translation: The fisherman was affected by ecstatic love, but he was also fearful. He had thus become doubly agitated. Now that his fear had subsided, however, he had become somewhat normal.

devanagari: स्वरूप कहे , - “याँरे तुमि कर ‘भूत’ - ज्ञान ।
भूत नहे - तेंहो कृष्ण - चैतन्य भगवान् ॥64॥
cc-antya-18.64.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara said to the fisherman, "My dear sir, the person whom you are thinking a ghost is not actually a ghost but the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: प्रेमावेशे पड़िला तेंहो समुद्रेर जले ।
ताँरे तुमि उठाइला आपनार जाले ॥65॥
cc-antya-18.65.translation: "Because of ecstatic love, the Lord fell into the sea, and you have caught Him in your net and rescued Him.

devanagari: ताँर स्पर्शे ह - इल तोमार कृष्ण - प्रेमोदय ।
भूत - प्रेत - ज्ञाने तोमार हैल महा - भय ॥66॥
cc-antya-18.66.translation: "Simply touching Him has awakened your dormant love of Kṛṣṇa, but because you thought Him a ghost, you were very much afraid of Him.

lines: ebe bhaya gela, tomāra mana haila sthire
devanagari: ‘एबे भय गेल, तोमार मन हैल स्थिरे ।
काहाँ ताँरे उठाञाछ, देखाह आमारे” ॥67॥
cc-antya-18.67.translation: "Now that your fear has gone and your mind is peaceful, please show me where He is."

devanagari: जालिया कहे , - “प्रभुरे देख्याछों बार - बार ।
तेंहो नहेन, एइ अति - विकृत आकार” ॥68॥
cc-antya-18.68.translation: The fisherman replied, "I have seen the Lord many times, but this is not He. This body is very deformed."

devanagari: स्वरूप कहे , - “ताँर हय प्रेमेर विकार ।
अस्थि - सन्धि छाड़े, हय अति दीर्घाकार” ॥69॥
cc-antya-18.69.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara said, "The Lord's body becomes transformed in His love for God. Sometimes the joints of His bones separate, and His body becomes very elongated."

lines: bhūme paḍi' kabhu mūrcchā, kabhu gaḍi' yāya
devanagari: कभु भावोन्मादे प्रभु इति - उति धाय ।
भूमे पड़ि’ कभु मूर्च्छा, कभु गड़ि’ याय ॥7॥
cc-antya-18.7.translation: He sometimes ran here and there in the madness of ecstasy and sometimes fell and rolled on the ground. Sometimes He became completely unconscious.

devanagari: शुनि, सेइ जालिया आनन्दित ह - इल ।
सबा ल ञा गेल, महाप्रभुरे देखाइल ॥70॥
cc-antya-18.70.translation: Hearing this, the fisherman was very happy. He brought all the devotees with him and showed them the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

lines: bhūmite paḍi' āche prabhu dīrgha saba kāya
devanagari: भूमिते पड़ि’ आछे प्रभु दीर्घ सब काय ।
जले श्वेत - तनु, वालु लागियाछे गाय ॥71॥
cc-antya-18.71.translation: The Lord was lying on the ground, His body elongated and bleached white by the water. He was covered from head to foot with sand.

lines: dūra patha uṭhāñā ghare ānāna nā yāya
devanagari: अति - दीर्घ शिथिल तनु - चर्म नट्काय ।
दूर पथ उठाञा घरे आनान ना याय ॥72॥
cc-antya-18.72.translation: The Lord's body was stretched, and His skin was slack and hanging loose. To lift Him and take Him the long distance home would have been impossible.

lines: ārdra kaupīna dūra kari' śuṣka parāñā
devanagari: आर्द्र कौपीन दूर करि’ शुष्क पराञा ।
बहिर्वासे शोयाइला वालुका छाड़ाञा ॥73॥
cc-antya-18.73.translation: The devotees removed His wet undergarment and replaced it with a dry one. Then, laying the Lord on an outer cloth, they cleaned the sand from His body.

lines: sabe meli' ucca kari' karena saṅkīrtane
ucca kari' kṛṣṇa-nāma kahena prabhura kāṇe
devanagari: सबे मेलि’ उच्च क रि’ करेन सङ्कीर्तने ।
उच्च क रि’ कृष्ण - नाम कहेन प्रभुर काणे ॥74॥
cc-antya-18.74.translation: They all performed saṅkīrtana, loudly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear.

devanagari: कत - क्षणे प्रभुर काणे शब्द परशिल ।
हुङ्कार करिया प्रभु तबहि उठिल ॥75॥
cc-antya-18.75.translation: After some time, the sound of the holy name entered the ear of the Lord, who immediately got up, making a great noise.

devanagari: उठितेइ अस्थि सब लागिल निज - स्थाने ।
‘अर्ध - बाह्ये’ इति - उति करेन दरशने ॥76॥
cc-antya-18.76.translation: As soon as He got up, His bones assumed their proper places. With half-external consciousness, the Lord looked here and there.

devanagari: तिन - दशाय महाप्रभु रहेन सर्व - काल ।
‘अन्तर्दशा’, ‘बाह्य - दशा’, ‘अर्ध - बाह्य’ आर ॥77॥
cc-antya-18.77.translation: The Lord remains in one of three different states of consciousness at all times: internal, external, and half-external.

devanagari: अन्तर्दशार किछु घोर, किछु बाह्य - ज्ञान ।
सेइ दशा कहे भक्त ‘अर्ध - बाह्य’ - नाम ॥78॥
cc-antya-18.78.translation: When the Lord is deeply absorbed in internal consciousness but He nevertheless exhibits some external consciousness, devotees call His condition ardha-bāhya, or half-external consciousness.

devanagari: ‘अर्ध - बाह्य’ कहेन प्रभु प्रलाप - वचने ।
आकाशे कहेन प्रभु, शुनेन भक्त - गणे ॥79॥
cc-antya-18.79.translation: In this half-external consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu talked like a madman. The devotees could distinctly hear Him speaking to the sky.

lines: rāsa-līlāra eka śloka yabe paḍe, śune
devanagari: रास - लीलार एक श्लोक यबे पड़े, शुने ।
पूर्ववत्तबे अर्थ करेन आपने ॥8॥
cc-antya-18.8.translation: When He heard Svarūpa Dāmodara recite a verse concerning the rāsa-līlā or He Himself recited one, He would personally explain it, as He had previously done.

devanagari: “कालिन्दी देखिया आमि गेलाङवृन्दावन ।
देखि, - जल - क्रीड़ा करेन व्रजेन्द्र - नन्दन ॥80॥
cc-antya-18.80.translation: "Seeing the River Yamunā," He said, "I went to Vṛndāvana. There I saw the son of Nanda Mahārāja performing His sporting pastimes in the water.

devanagari: राधिकादि गोपी - गण - सङ्गे एकत्र मेलि’ ।
यमुनार जले महा - रङ्गे करेन केलि ॥81॥
cc-antya-18.81.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa was in the water of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs, headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. They were performing pastimes in a great sporting manner.

devanagari: तीरे रहि’ देखि आमि सखी - गण - सङ्गे।
एक - सखी सखी - गणे देखाय सेइ रङ्गे ॥82॥
cc-antya-18.82.translation: "I saw this pastime as I stood on the bank of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs. One gopī was showing some other gopīs the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the water.

devanagari: पट्ट - वस्त्र, अलङ्कारे, समर्पिया सखी - करे,
सूक्ष्म - शुक्ल - वस्त्र - परिधान ।
कृष्ण लञा कान्ता - गण, कैला जलावगाहन ,
जल - केलि रचिला सुठाम ॥83॥
cc-antya-18.83.translation: "All the gopīs entrusted their silken garments and ornaments to the care of their friends and then put on fine white cloth. Taking His beloved gopīs with Him, Lord Kṛṣṇa bathed and performed very nice pastimes in the water of the Yamunā.

devanagari: सखि हे, देख कृष्णेर जल - केलि - रङ्गे
कृष्ण मत्त करि - वर, चञ्चल कर - पुष्कर, ।
गोपी - गण करिणीर सङ्गे ॥84॥
cc-antya-18.84.translation: "My dear friends, just see Lord Kṛṣṇa's sporting pastimes in the water. Kṛṣṇa's restless palms resemble lotus flowers. He is just like a chief of mad elephants, and the gopīs who accompany Him are like she-elephants.

devanagari: आरम्भिला जल - केलि, अन्यो’न्ये जल फेलाफेलि ,
हुड़ाहुड़ि, वर्षे जल - धार ।
सबे जय - पराजय, नाहि किछु निश्चय,
जल - युद्ध बाड़िल अपार ॥85॥
cc-antya-18.85.translation: "The sporting pastimes in the water began, and everyone started splashing water back and forth. In the tumultuous showers of water, no one could be certain which party was winning and which was losing. This sporting water fight increased unlimitedly.

lines: varṣe sthira taḍid-gaṇa, siñce śyāma nava-ghana,
devanagari: वर्षे स्थिर तड़िगण, सिञ्चे श्याम नव - धन
घन वर्षे तड़ित् उपरे ।
सखी - गणेर नयन, तृषित चातक - गण
सेइ अमृत सुखे पान करे ॥86॥
cc-antya-18.86.translation: "The gopīs were like steady streaks of lightning, and Kṛṣṇa resembled a blackish cloud. The lightning began sprinkling water upon the cloud, and the cloud upon the lightning. Like thirsty cātaka birds, the eyes of the gopīs joyously drank the nectarean water from the cloud.

devanagari: प्रथमे युद्ध ‘जलाजलि’, तबे युद्ध कराकरि’
तार पाछे युद्ध ‘मुखामुखि’ ।
तबे युद्ध ‘हृदाहृदि’, तबे हैल ‘रदारदि’
तबे हैल युद्ध ‘नखान खि’ ॥87॥
cc-antya-18.87.translation: "As the fight began, they splashed water on one another. Then they fought hand to hand, then face to face, then chest to chest, teeth to teeth and finally nail to nail.

lines: sahasra-kare jala seke, sahasra netre gopī dekhe,
devanagari: सहस्र - करे जल सेके, सहस्र नेत्रे गोपी देखे
सहस्र - पदे निकट गमने ।
सहस्र - मुख - चुम्बने, सहस्त्र - वपु - सङ्गमे
गोपी - नर्म शुने सहस्र - काणे ॥88॥
cc-antya-18.88.translation: "Thousands of hands splashed water, and the gopīs saw Kṛṣṇa with thousands of eyes. With thousands of legs they came near Him and kissed Him with thousands of faces. Thousands of bodies embraced Him. The gopīs heard His joking words with thousands of ears.

lines: kṛṣṇa rādhā lañā bale, gelā kaṇṭha-daghna jale,
teṅho kṛṣṇa-kaṇṭha dhari', bhāse jalera upari,
devanagari: कृष्ण राधा लञा बले, गेला कण्ठ - दघ्न जले ,
छाड़िला ताहाँ, याहाँ अगाध पानी ।
तेंहो कृष्ण - कण्ठ ध रि’, भासे जलेर उपरि ,
गजोखाते यैछे कमलिनी ॥89॥
cc-antya-18.89.translation: "Kṛṣṇa forcibly swept Rādhārāṇī away and took Her into water up to Her neck. Then He released Her where the water was very deep. She grasped Kṛṣṇa's neck, however, and floated on the water like a lotus flower plucked by the trunk of a elephant.

lines: sabāra artha kare, pāya kabhu harṣa-śoka
devanagari: एइ - मत रास - लीलाय हय यत श्लोक ।
सबार अर्थ करे, पाय कभु हर्ष - शोक ॥9॥
cc-antya-18.9.translation: In this way, He explained the meaning of all the verses concerning the rāsa-līlā. Sometimes He would be very sad and sometimes very happy.

lines: yata gopa-sundarī, kṛṣṇa tata rūpa dhari',
devanagari: यत गोप - सुन्दरी, कृष्ण तत रूप धरि’
सबार वस्त्र करिला हरणे ।
यमुना - जल निर्मल, अङ्ग करे झलमल
सुखे कृष्ण करे दरशने ॥90॥
cc-antya-18.90.translation: "Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself into as many forms as there were gopīs and then took away all the garments that covered them. The water of the River Yamunā was crystal clear, and Kṛṣṇa saw the glittering bodies of the gopīs in great happiness.

devanagari: पद्मिनी - लता - सखी - चय, कैल कारो सहाय
तरङ्ग - हस्ते पत्र समर्पिल ।
केह मुक्त - केश - पाश, आगे कैल अधोवास
हस्ते केह कञ्जलि धरिल ॥91॥
cc-antya-18.91.translation: "The lotus stems were friends of the gopīs and therefore helped them by offering them lotus leaves. The lotuses pushed their large, round leaves over the surface of the water with their hands, the waves of the Yamunā, to cover the gopīs' bodies. Some gopīs undid their hair and kept it in front of them as dresses to cover the lower portions of their bodies and used their hands as bodices to cover their breasts.

lines: ākaṇṭha-vapu jale paiśe, mukha-mātra jale bhāse,
devanagari: कृष्णेर कलह राधा - सने, गोपी - गण सेइ - क्षणे
हेमाब्ज - वने गेला लुकाइते ।
आकण्ठ - वपु जले पैशे, मुख - मात्र जले भासे
पद्म - मुखे ना पारि चिनिते ॥92॥
cc-antya-18.92.translation: "Then Kṛṣṇa quarreled with Rādhārāṇī, and all the gopīs hid themselves in a cluster of white lotus flowers. They submerged their bodies up to their necks in the water. Only their faces floated above the surface, and the faces were indistinguishable from the lotuses.

lines: ethā kṛṣṇa rādhā-sane, kailā ye āchila mane,
tabe rādhā sūkṣma-mati, jāniyā sakhīra sthiti,
devanagari: एथा कृष्ण राधा - सने, कैला ये आछिल मने
गोपी - गण अन्वेषिते गेला ।
तबे राधा सूक्ष्म - मति, जानिया सखीर स्थिति
सखी - मध्ये आसिया मिलिला ॥93॥
cc-antya-18.93.translation: "In the absence of the other gopīs, Lord Kṛṣṇa behaved with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī as freely as He desired. When the gopīs began searching for Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, being of very fine intelligence and thus knowing the situation of Her friends, immediately mingled in their midst.

lines: yata hemābja jale bhāse, tata nīlābja tāra pāśe,
nīlābje hemābje ṭheke, yuddha haya pratyeke,
devanagari: यत हेमाब्ज जले भासे, तत नीलाब्ज तार पाशे
आसि’ आसि’ करये मिलन ।
नीलाब्जे हेमाब्जे ठेके, युद्ध हय प्रत्येके
कौतुके देखे तीरे सखी - गण ॥94॥
cc-antya-18.94.translation: "Many white lotus flowers were floating in the water, and as many bluish lotus flowers came nearby. As they came close together, the white and blue lotuses collided and began fighting with one another. The gopīs on the bank of the Yamunā watched with great amusement.

devanagari: चक्रवाक - मण्डल, पृथक्पृथक् झुगल
जल हैते करिल उद्गम ।
उठिल पद्म - मण्डल, पृथक्पृथक् युगल
चक्रवाके कैल आच्छादन ॥95॥
cc-antya-18.95.translation: "When the raised breasts of the gopīs, which resembled the globelike bodies of cakravāka birds, emerged from the water in separate couples, the bluish lotuses of Kṛṣṇa's hands rose to cover them.

lines: uṭhila bahu raktotpala, pṛthak pṛthak yugala,
devanagari: उठिल बहु रक्तोत्पल, पृथक्पृथक् युगल
पद्म - गणेर कैल निवारण ।
‘पद्म’ चाहे लुटि’ निते, ‘उत्पल’ चाहे राखिते’
‘चक्रवाक’ लागि’ दुँहार रण ॥96॥
cc-antya-18.96.translation: "The hands of the gopīs, which resembled red lotus flowers, arose from the water in pairs to obstruct the bluish flowers. The blue lotuses tried to plunder the white cakravāka birds, and the red lotuses tried to protect them. Thus there was a fight between the two.

lines: ihāṅ duṅhāra ulṭā sthiti, dharma haila viparīti,
devanagari: पद्मोत्पल - अचेतन, चक्रवाक सचेतन
चक्रवाके पद्म आस्वादय ।
इहाँ दुँहार उल्टा स्थिति, धर्म हैल विपरीति
कृष्णेर राज्ये ऐछे न्याय हय ॥97॥
cc-antya-18.97.translation: "Blue and red lotus flowers are unconscious objects, whereas cakravākas are conscious and alive. Nevertheless, in ecstatic love, the blue lotuses began to taste the cakravākas. This is a reversal of their natural behavior, but in Lord Kṛṣṇa's kingdom such reversals are a principle of His pastimes.

lines: mitrera mitra saha-vāsī, cakravāke luṭe āsi',
aparicita śatrura mitra, rākhe utpala,—e baḍa citra,
devanagari: मित्रेर मित्र सह - वासी, चक्रवाके लुटे आसि’,
कृष्णेर राज्ये ऐछे व्यवहार ।
अपरिचित शत्रुर मित्र, राखे उत्पल , - ए बड़ चित्र ,
एइ बड़ ‘विरोध - अलङ्कार’ ॥98॥
cc-antya-18.98.translation: "The blue lotuses are friends of the sun-god, and though they all live together, the blue lotuses plunder the cakravākas. The red lotuses, however, blossom at night and are therefore strangers or enemies to the cakravākas. Yet in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes the red lotuses, which are the hands of the gopīs, protect their cakravāka breasts. This is a metaphor of contradiction."

lines: yāhā kari' āsvādana, ānandita mora mana,
devanagari: अतिशयोक्ति, विरोधाभास, दुइ अलङ्कार प्रकाश,
करि’ कृष्ण प्रकट देखाइल ।
याहा क रि’ आस्वादन, आनन्दित मोर मन ,
नेत्र - कर्ण - युग्म जुड़ाइल ॥99॥
cc-antya-18.99.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "In His pastimes, Kṛṣṇa displayed the two ornaments of hyperbole and reverse analogy. Tasting them brought gladness to My mind and fully satisfied My ears and eyes.

devanagari: वन्दे तं कृष्ण - चैतन्यं मातृ - भक्त - शिरोमणिम् ।
प्रलप्य मुख - सङ्घर्षी मधूद्याने ललास यः ॥1॥
cc-antya-19.1.translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most exalted of all devotees of mothers, spoke like a madman and rubbed His face against the walls. Overwhelmed by emotions of ecstatic love, He would sometimes enter the Jagannātha-vallabha garden to perform His pastimes. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.

lines: ei aparādha tumi nā la-iha āmāra
devanagari: एइ अपराध तुमि ना ल - इह आमार ।
तोमार अधीन आमि - पुत्र से तोमार ॥10॥
cc-antya-19.10.translation: "Mother, please do not take this as an offense, for I, your son, am completely dependent upon you.

lines: svarūpa-rāmānanda gāya, prabhu nāce, sukha pāya,
devanagari: स्वरूप - रामानन्द गाय, प्रभु नाचे, सुख पाय,
एइ - मते प्रातः - काल है ल ।
स्वरूप - रामानन्द - राय, करि नाना उपाय ,
महाप्रभुर बाह्य - स्फूर्ति कैल ॥100॥
cc-antya-19.100.translation: Both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya sang to the Lord, who danced and enjoyed happiness until the morning arrived. Then they devised a plan to revive the Lord to external consciousness.

devanagari: मातृ - भक्ति, प्रलापन, भित्त्ये मुख - घर्षण ,
कृष्ण - गन्ध - स्फूर्ये दिव्य - नृत्य ।
एइ चारि - लीला - भेदे, गाइल एइ परिच्छेदे ,
कृष्णदास रूप - गोसाञि - भृत्य ॥101॥
cc-antya-19.101.translation: Thus, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, have sung of four divisions of the Lord's pastimes in this chapter: the Lord's devotion to His mother, His words of madness, His rubbing His face against the walls at night, and His dancing at the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa's fragrance.

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु पाञा चेतन ।
स्नान क रि’ कैल जगन्नाथ - दरशन ॥102॥
cc-antya-19.102.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus returned to consciousness. He then bathed and went to see Lord Jagannātha.

devanagari: अलौकिक कृष्ण - लीला, दिव्य - शक्ति तार ।
तकर्ेर गोचर नहे चरित्र याहार ॥103॥
cc-antya-19.103.translation: The pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are uncommonly full of transcendental potency. It is a characteristic of such pastimes that they do not fall within the jurisdiction of experimental logic and arguments.

lines: ei prema sadā jāge yāhāra antare
paṇḍiteha tāra ceṣṭā bujhite nā pāre
devanagari: एइ प्रेम सदा जागे याहार अन्तरे ।
पण्डितेह तार चेष्टा बुझिते ना पारे ॥104॥
cc-antya-19.104.translation: When transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa awakens in one's heart, even a learned scholar cannot comprehend one's activities.

devanagari: धन्यस्यायं नवः प्रेमा यस्योन्मीलति चेतसि ।
अन्तर्वाणीभिरप्यस्य मुद्रा सुष्ठ सु - दुर्गमा ॥105॥
cc-antya-19.105.translation: "The activities and symptoms of that exalted personality in whose heart love of Godhead has awakened cannot be understood even by the most learned scholar."

lines: tarka nā kariha, śuna viśvāsa kariyā
devanagari: अलौकिक प्रभुर चेष्टा’, ‘प्रलाप’ शुनिया ।
तकर् ना करिह, शुन विश्वास करिया ॥106॥
cc-antya-19.106.translation: The activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are undoubtedly uncommon, especially His talking like a madman. Therefore, one who hears of these pastimes should not put forward mundane arguments. He should simply hear the pastimes with full faith.

devanagari: इहार सत्यत्वे प्रमाण श्री - भागवते ।
श्री - राधार प्रेम - प्रलाप ‘भ्रमर - गीता’ ते ॥107॥
cc-antya-19.107.translation: The evidence of the truth of these talks is found in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. There, in the section of the Tenth Canto known as the Bhramara-gītā, "the Song to the Bumblebee," Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī speaks insanely in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: महिषीर गीत येन ‘दशमे’र शेषे ।
पण्डिते ना बुझे तार अर्थ - विशेषे ॥108॥
cc-antya-19.108.translation: The songs of the queens at Dvārakā, which are mentioned at the end of the Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, have a very special meaning. They are not understood even by the most learned scholars.

lines: yāre kṛpā karena, tāra haya ithe viśvāsa
devanagari: महाप्रभु - नित्यानन्द, दोंहार दासेर दास ।
यारे कृपा करेन, तार हय इथे विश्वास ॥109॥
cc-antya-19.109.translation: If one becomes a servant of the servants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and is favored by Them, he can believe in all these discourses.

lines: yāvat jība, tāvat āmi nāriba chāḍite'
devanagari: नीलाचले आछि आमि तोमार आज्ञाते ।
यावत् जीब, तावतामि नारिब छाड़िते” ॥11॥
cc-antya-19.11.translation: "I am staying here at Nīlācala, Jagannātha Purī, according to your order. As long as I live, I shall not leave this place.' "

lines: śraddhā kari, śuna ihā, śunite mahā-sukha
devanagari: श्रद्धा करि, शुन इहा, शुनिते महा - सुख ।
खण्डिबे आध्यात्मिकादि कुतर्कादि - दुःख ॥110॥
cc-antya-19.110.translation: Just try to hear these topics with faith, for there is great pleasure even in hearing them. That hearing will destroy all miseries pertaining to the body, mind and other living entities, and the unhappiness of false arguments as well.

devanagari: चैतन्य - चरितामृत - नित्य - नूतन ।
शुनिते शुनिते जुड़ाय हृदय - श्रवण ॥111॥
cc-antya-19.111.translation: Caitanya-caritāmṛta is ever-increasingly fresh. Continuously hearing it pacifies one's heart and ear.

devanagari: श्री - रूप - रघुनाथ - पदे यार आश ।
चैतन्य - चरितामृत कहे कृष्णदास ॥112॥
cc-antya-19.112.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

devanagari: गोप - लीलाय पाइला येइ प्रसाद - वसने ।
मातारे पाठान ताहा पुरीर वचने ॥12॥
cc-antya-19.12.translation: Following the order of Paramānanda Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sent His mother the prasāda clothing left by Lord Jagannātha after His pastimes as a cowherd boy.

devanagari: जगन्नाथेर उत्तम प्रसाद आनिया यतने ।
मातारे पृथक् पाठान्, आर भक्त - गणे ॥13॥
cc-antya-19.13.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very carefully brought first-class prasāda from Lord Jagannātha and sent it in separate packages to His mother and the devotees at Nadia.

devanagari: मातृ - भक्त - गणेर प्रभु हन शिरोमणि ।
सन्यास करिया सदा सेवेन जननी ॥14॥
cc-antya-19.14.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the topmost gem of all devotees of mothers. He rendered service to His mother even after He had accepted the vow of sannyāsa.

devanagari: जगदानन्द नदीया गिया मातारे मिलिला ।
प्रभुर यत निवेदन, सकल कहिला ॥15॥
cc-antya-19.15.translation: Jagadānanda Paṇḍita thus returned to Nadia, and when he met Śacīmātā, he conveyed to her all the Lord's salutations.

devanagari: आचार्यादि भक्त - गणे मिलिला प्रसाद दिया ।
माता - ठाञि आज्ञा ल - इला मासेक रहिया ॥16॥
cc-antya-19.16.translation: He then met all the other devotees, headed by Advaita Ācārya, and gave them the prasāda of Jagannātha. After staying for one month, he took permission from mother Śacī to leave.

devanagari: आचार्येर ठाञि गिया आज्ञा मागिला ।
आचार्य - गोसाञि प्रभुरे सन्देश कहिला ॥17॥
cc-antya-19.17.translation: When he went to Advaita Ācārya and also asked His permission to return, Advaita Prabhu gave him a message to deliver to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

lines: prabhu mātra bujhena, keha bujhite nā pāre
devanagari: तरजा - प्रहेली आचार्य कहेन ठारे - ठोरे ।
प्रभु मात्र बुझेन, केह बुझिते ना पारे ॥18॥
cc-antya-19.18.translation: Advaita Ācārya had written a sonnet in equivocal language with an import that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could understand but others could not.

devanagari: “प्रभुरे कहिह आमार कोटि नमस्कार ।
एइ निवेदन ताँर चरणे आमार ॥19॥
cc-antya-19.19.translation: In His sonnet, Advaita Prabhu first offered His obeisances hundreds and thousands of times unto the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He then submitted the following statement at His lotus feet.

devanagari: जय जय श्री - चैतन्य जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैत - चन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-antya-19.2.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

devanagari: बाउलके कहिह , - लोक ह - इल बाउल ।
बाउलके कहिह , - हाटे ना विकाय चाउल ॥20॥
cc-antya-19.20.translation: "Please inform Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is acting like a madman, that everyone here has become mad like Him. Inform Him also that in the marketplace, rice is no longer in demand.

devanagari: बाउलके कहिह , - काये नाहिक आउल ।
बाउलके कहिह , - इहा कहियाछे बाउल” ॥21॥
cc-antya-19.21.translation: "Those now mad in ecstatic love are no longer interested in the material world. Tell Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that Advaita Prabhu, who has also become a madman in ecstatic love, has spoken these words."

devanagari: एत शुनि’ जगदानन्द हासिते लागिला ।
नीलाचले आ सि’ तबे प्रभुरे कहिला ॥22॥
cc-antya-19.22.translation: When he heard Advaita Ācārya's statement, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita began to laugh, and when he returned to Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala, he informed Caitanya Mahāprabhu of everything.

devanagari: तरजा शुनि’ महाप्रभु ईषत् हासिला ।
‘ताँर येइ आज्ञा ‘ - बलि’ मौन धरिला ॥23॥
cc-antya-19.23.translation: After hearing the equivocal sonnet by Advaita Ācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu quietly smiled. "That is His order," He said. Then He fell silent.

devanagari: जानियाओ स्वरूप गोसाञि प्रभुरे पुछिल ।
‘एइ तरजार अर्थ बुझिते नारिल’ ॥24॥
cc-antya-19.24.translation: Although he knew the secret, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī inquired from the Lord, "What is the meaning of this sonnet? I could not understand it."

devanagari: प्रभु कहेन, - ‘आचार्य हय पूजक प्रबल ।
आगम - शास्त्रेर विधि - विधाने कुशल ॥25॥
cc-antya-19.25.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Advaita Ācārya is a great worshiper of the Lord and is very expert in the regulative principles enjoined in the Vedic literatures.

lines: pūjā lāgi' kata kāla karena nirodhana
devanagari: उपासना ला गि’ देवेर करेन आवाहन ।
पूजा लागि’ कत काल करेन निरोधन ॥26॥
cc-antya-19.26.translation: "Advaita Ācārya invites the Lord to come and be worshiped, and to perform the worship He keeps the Deity for some time.

lines: tarajāra nā jāni artha, kibā tāṅra mana
devanagari: पूजा - निर्वाहण हैले पाछे करेन विसर्जन ।
तरजार ना जानि अर्थ, किबा ताँर मन ॥27॥
cc-antya-19.27.translation: "After the worship is completed, He sends the Deity somewhere else. I do not know the meaning of this sonnet, nor do I know what is in Advaita Prabhu's mind.

devanagari: महा - योगेश्वर आचार्य - तरजाते समर्थ ।
आमिह बुझिते नारि तरजार अर्थ’ ॥28॥
cc-antya-19.28.translation: "Advaita Ācārya is a great mystic. No one can understand Him. He is expert in writing sonnets that even I Myself cannot understand."

devanagari: शुनिया विस्मित ह - इला सब भक्त - गण ।
स्वरूप - गोसाञि किछु ह - इला विमन ॥29॥
cc-antya-19.29.translation: Hearing this, all the devotees were astonished, especially Svarūpa Dāmodara, who became somewhat morose.

devanagari: एइ - मते महाप्रभु कृष्ण - प्रेमावेशे ।
उन्माद - प्रलाप करे रात्रि - दिवसे ॥3॥
cc-antya-19.3.translation: In the ecstasy of love of Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus behaved like a madman, talking insanely all day and night.

lines: sei dina haite prabhura āra daśā ha-ila
devanagari: सेइ दिन हैते प्रभुर आर दशा ह - इल ।
कृष्णेर विच्छेद - दशा द्विगुण बाड़िल ॥30॥
cc-antya-19.30.translation: From that day on, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's emotional state changed markedly; His feelings of separation from Kṛṣṇa doubled in intensity.

devanagari: उन्माद - प्रलाप - चेष्टा करे रात्रि - दिने ।
राधा - भावावेशे विरह बाड़े अनुक्षणे ॥31॥
cc-antya-19.31.translation: As His feelings of separation in the ecstasy of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī increased at every moment, the Lord's activities, both day and night, were now wild, insane performances.

devanagari: आचम्बिते स्फुरे कृष्णेर मथुरा - गमन ।
उद्धुर्णा - दशा हैल उन्माद - लक्षण ॥32॥
cc-antya-19.32.translation: Suddenly there awoke within Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the scene of Lord Kṛṣṇa's departure to Mathurā, and He began exhibiting the symptom of ecstatic madness known as udghūrṇā.

devanagari: रामानन्देर गला ध रि’ करेन प्रलापन ।
स्वरूपे पुछेन मानि’ निज - सखी - गण ॥33॥
cc-antya-19.33.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke like a madman, holding Rāmānanda Rāya by the neck, and He questioned Svarūpa Dāmodara, thinking him to be His gopī friend.

lines: sei śloka paḍi' pralāpa karite lāgilā
devanagari: पूर्वे येन विशाखारे राधिका पुछिला ।
सेइ श्लोक प ड़ि’ प्रलाप करिते लागिला ॥34॥
cc-antya-19.34.translation: Just as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī inquired from Her personal friend Viśākhā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, reading that very verse, began speaking like a madman.

lines: nidhir mama suhṛttamaḥ kva bata hanta hā dhig-vidhim
devanagari: क्व नन्द - कुल - चन्द्रमाः क्व शिखि - चन्द्रकालङ्कतिः क्व मन्द्र - मुरली - रवः क्व नु सुरेन्द्र - नील - द्युतिः ।
क्व रास - रस - ताण्डवी क्व सखि जीव - रक्षौषधिर् निधिर्मम सुहृत्तमः क्व बत हन्त हा धिग्विधिम् ॥35॥
cc-antya-19.35.translation: "My dear friend, where is Kṛṣṇa, who is like the moon rising from the ocean of Mahārāja Nanda's dynasty? Where is Kṛṣṇa, His head decorated with a peacock feather? Where is He? Where is Kṛṣṇa, whose flute produces such a deep sound? Oh, where is Kṛṣṇa, whose bodily luster is like the luster of the blue indranīla jewel? Where is Kṛṣṇa, who is so expert in rāsa dancing? Oh, where is He who can save My life? Kindly tell Me where to find Kṛṣṇa, the treasure of My life and best of My friends. Feeling separation from Him, I hereby condemn Providence, the shaper of My destiny.'

lines: kānty-amṛta yebā piye, nirantara piyā jiye,
devanagari: व्रजेन्द्र - कुल दुग्ध - सिन्धु, कृष्ण ताहे पूर्ण इन्दु
जन्मि’ कैला जगत् उजोर ।
कान्त्यमृत ग्रेबा पिये, निरन्तर पिया जिये
व्रज - जनेर नयन - चकोर ॥36॥
cc-antya-19.36.translation: "The family of Mahārāja Nanda is just like an ocean of milk, wherein Lord Kṛṣṇa has arisen like the full moon to illuminate the entire universe. The eyes of the residents of Vraja are like cakora birds that continuously drink the nectar of His bodily luster and thus live peacefully.

lines: sakhi he, kothā kṛṣṇa, karāha daraśana
kṣaṇeke yāhāra mukha, nā dekhile phāṭe buka,
devanagari: सखि हे, कोथा कृष्ण, कराह दरशन
क्षणेके याहार मुख, ना देखिले फाटे बुक, ।
शीघ्र देखाह, ना रहे जीवन ॥37॥
cc-antya-19.37.translation: "My dear friend, where is Kṛṣṇa? Kindly let Me see Him. My heart breaks at not seeing His face even for a moment. Kindly show Him to Me immediately; otherwise I cannot live.

lines: praphullita kare yei, kāhāṅ mora candra sei,
devanagari: एइ व्रजेर रमणी, कामाकर् - तप्त - कुमुदिनी,
निज - करामृत दिया दान ।
प्रफुल्लित करे येइ, काहाँ मोर चन्द्र सेइ ,
देखाह, सखि, राख मोर प्राण ॥38॥
cc-antya-19.38.translation: "The women of Vṛndāvana are just like lilies growing hot in the sun of lusty desires. But moonlike Kṛṣṇa makes them all jubilant by bestowing upon them the nectar of His hands. O My dear friend, where is My moon now? Save My life by showing Him to Me!

lines: kāhāṅ se cūḍāra ṭhāma, śikhi-piñchera uḍāna,
devanagari: काहाँ से चूड़ार ठाम, शिखि - पिञ्छेर उड़ान
नव - मेघे येन इन्द्र - धनु ।
पीताम्बर - तड़ियुति, मुक्ता - माला - बक - पाँति
नवाम्बुद जिनि’ श्याम - तनु ॥39॥
cc-antya-19.39.translation: "My dear friend, where is that beautiful helmet with a peacock feather upon it like a rainbow upon a new cloud? Where are those yellow garments, shining like lightning? And where is that necklace of pearls that resemble flocks of ducks flying in the sky? The blackish body of Kṛṣṇa triumphs over the new blackish rain cloud.

devanagari: प्रभुर अत्यन्त प्रिय पण्डित - जगदानन्द ।
याहार चरित्रे प्रभु पायेन आनन्द ॥4॥
cc-antya-19.4.translation: Jagadānanda Paṇḍita was a very dear devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord derived great pleasure from his activities.

lines: eka-bāra yāra nayane lāge, sadā tāra hṛdaye jāge,
nārī-mane paiśe hāya, yatne nāhi bāhirāya,
devanagari: एक - बार यार नयने लागे, सदा तार हृदये जागे ,
कृष्ण - तनु - येन आम्र - आठा ।
नारी - मने पैशे हाय, यत्न नाहि बाहिराय ,
तनु नहे, - सेया - कुलेर काँटा ॥40॥
cc-antya-19.40.translation: "If a person's eyes even once capture that beautiful body of Kṛṣṇa's, it remains always prominent within his heart. Kṛṣṇa's body resembles the sap of the mango tree, for when it enters the minds of women, it will not come out, despite great endeavor. Thus Kṛṣṇa's extraordinary body is like a thorn of the seyā berry tree.

devanagari: जिनिया तमाल - द्युति, इन्द्रनील - सम कान्ति
से कान्तिते जगत्माताय ।
श्रङ्गार - रस - सार छा नि’, ताते चन्द्र - ज्योत्स्ना सा नि’
जानि विधि निरमिला ताय ॥41॥
cc-antya-19.41.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's bodily luster shines like the indranīla gem and surpasses the luster of the tamāla tree. The luster of His body drives the entire world mad because Providence has made it transparent by refining the essence of the mellow of conjugal love and mixing it with moonshine.

devanagari: काहाँ से मुरली - ध्वनि, नवाभ्र - गर्जित जि नि’
जगताकर्षे श्रवणे याहार ।
उठि’ धाय व्रज - जन, तृषित चातक - गण
आसि’ पिये कान्त्यमृत - धार ॥42॥
cc-antya-19.42.translation: "The deep vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute surpasses the thundering of new clouds and attracts the aural reception of the entire world. Thus the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana rise and pursue that sound, drinking the showering nectar of Kṛṣṇa's bodily luster like thirsty cātaka birds.

lines: deha jīye tāṅhā vine, dhik ei jīvane,
devanagari: “मोर सेइ कला - निधि, प्राण - रक्षा - महौषधि ,
सखि, मोर तेंहो सुहृत्तम ।
देह जीये ताँहा विने, धिक् एइ जीवने,
विधि करे एत विड़म्बन !” ॥43॥
cc-antya-19.43.translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the reservoir of art and culture, and He is the panacea that saves My life. O My dear friend, since I live without Him, who is the best among My friends, I condemn the duration of My life. I think that Providence has cheated Me in many ways.

lines: 'ye-jana jīte nāhi cāya, tāre kene jīyāya',
vidhire kare bhartsana, kṛṣṇe dena olāhana,
devanagari: ‘ये - जन जीते नाहि चाय, तारे केने जीया य’
विधि - प्रति उठे क्रोध - शोक ।
विधिरे करे भर्सन, कृष्णे देन ओलाहन
पड़ि’ भागवतेर एक श्लोक ॥44॥
cc-antya-19.44.translation: "Why does Providence continue the life of one who does not wish to live?" This thought aroused anger and lamentation. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then read a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam that chastises Providence and makes an accusation against Kṛṣṇa.

lines: aho vidhātas tava na kvacid dayā
devanagari: अहो विधातस्तव न क्वचिद्दया संयोज्य मैत्र्या प्रणयेन देहिनः ।
तांश्चाकृतार्थान्वियुनङ्क्ष्यपार्थकं विचेष्टितं तेऽर्भक - चेष्टितं यथा ॥45॥
cc-antya-19.45.translation: “ 'O Providence, you have no mercy! You bring embodied souls together through friendship and affection, but before their desires are fulfilled, you separate them. Your activities are like the foolish pranks of children.'

lines: 'tora yadi lāg pāiye, tabe tore śikṣā diye,
devanagari: “ना जानिस् प्रेम - मर्म, व्यर्थ करिस् परिश्रम
तोर चेष्टा - बालक - समान ।
तोर यदि लाग् पाइये, तबे तोरे शिक्षा दिये
एमन येन ना करिस् विधान ॥46॥
cc-antya-19.46.translation: "Providence, you do not know the purport of loving affairs, and therefore you baffle all our endeavors. This is very childish of you. If we could catch you, we would give you such a lesson that you would never again make such arrangements.

lines: anyo 'nya durlabha jana, preme karāñā sammilana,
devanagari: अरे विधि, तुइ बड़ - इ निठुर
अन्यो’न्य दुर्लभ जन, प्रेमे करा ञा सम्मिलन, ।
‘अकृतार्थान्’ केने करिस् दूर? ॥47॥
cc-antya-19.47.translation: "Oh, cruel Providence! You are very unkind, for you bring together in love people who are rarely in touch with each other. Then, after you have made them meet but before they are fulfilled, you again spread them far apart.

lines: kṣaṇeke karite pāna, kāḍi' nilā anya sthāna,
devanagari: अरे विधि अकरुण, देखाञा कृष्णानन
नेत्र - मन लोभाइला मोर ।
क्षणेके करिते पान, काड़ि’ निला अन्य स्थान
पाप कैलि ‘दत्त - अपहार’ ॥48॥
cc-antya-19.48.translation: "O Providence, you are so unkind! You reveal the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa and make the mind and eyes greedy, but after they have drunk that nectar for only a moment, you whisk Kṛṣṇa away to another place. This is a great sin because you thus take away what you have given as charity.

lines: 'akrūra kare tomāra doṣa, āmāya kene kara roṣa',
tui akrūra-mūrti dhari', kṛṣṇa nili curi kari',
devanagari: ‘अक्रूर करे तोमार दोष, आमाय केने कर रोष’
इहा यदि कह ‘दुराचार’ ।
तुइ अक्रूर - मूर्ति धरि’, कृष्ण निलि चुरि करि’
अन्येर नहे ऐछे व्यवहार ॥49॥
cc-antya-19.49.translation: "O misbehaved Providence! If you reply to us, 'Akrūra is actually at fault; why are you angry with me?' then I say to you, 'Providence, you have taken the form of Akrūra and have stolen Kṛṣṇa away. No one else would behave like this.'

devanagari: प्रति - वत्सर प्रभु ताँरे पाठान नदीयाते ।
विच्छेद - दुःखिता जानि’ जननी आश्वासिते ॥5॥
cc-antya-19.5.translation: Knowing His mother to be greatly afflicted by separation, the Lord would send Jagadānanda Paṇḍita to Navadvīpa every year to console her.

lines: āpanāra karma-doṣa, tore kibā kari roṣa,
ye āmāra prāṇa-nātha, ekatra rahi yāṅra sātha,
devanagari: आपनार कर्म - दोष, तोरे किबा करि रोष
तोय - मोय सम्बन्ध विदूर ।
ये आमार प्राण - नाथ, एकत्र रहि यॉर साथ
सेइ कृष्ण ह - इला निठुर! ॥50॥
cc-antya-19.50.translation: "But this is the fault of My own destiny. Why should I needlessly accuse you? There is no intimate relationship between you and Me. Kṛṣṇa, however, is My life and soul. It is We who live together, and it is He who has become so cruel.

lines: saba tyaji' bhaji yāṅre, sei āpana-hāte māre,
tāṅra lāgi' āmi mari, ulaṭi' nā cāhe hari,
devanagari: सब त्यजि’ भजि याँरे, सेइ आपन - हाते मारे
नारी - वधे कृष्णेर नाहि भय ।
ताँर ला गि’ आमि मरि, उलटि’ ना चाहे हरि
क्षण - मात्रे भाङ्गिल प्रणय ॥51॥
cc-antya-19.51.translation: "He for whom I have left everything is personally killing Me with His own hands. Kṛṣṇa has no fear of killing women. Indeed, I am dying for Him, but He doesn't even turn back to look at Me. Within a moment, He has broken off our loving affairs.

lines: kṛṣṇe kene kari roṣa, āpana durdaiva-doṣa,
ye kṛṣṇa—mora premādhīna, tāre kaila udāsīna,
devanagari: कृष्णे केने करि रोष, आपन दुर्दैव - दोष
पाकिल मोर एइ पाप - फल ।
ये कृष्ण - मोर प्रेमाधीन, तारे कैल उदासीन
एइ मोर अभाग्य प्रबल” ॥52॥
cc-antya-19.52.translation: "Yet why should I be angry with Kṛṣṇa? It is the fault of My own misfortune. The fruit of my sinful activities has ripened, and therefore Kṛṣṇa, who has always been dependent on My love, is now indifferent. This means that My misfortune is very strong."

lines: ei-mata gaura-rāya, viṣāde kare hāya hāya,
devanagari: एइ - मत गौर - राय, विषादे करे हाय हाय ,
‘हा हा कृष्ण, तुमि गेला कति?’।
गोपी - भाव हृदये, तार वाक्ये विलापये ,
‘गोविन्द दामोदर माधवेति’ ॥53॥
cc-antya-19.53.translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented in the mood of separation, "Alas, alas! O Kṛṣṇa, where have You gone?" Feeling in His heart the ecstatic emotions of the gopīs, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu agonized in their words, saying, "O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!"

devanagari: तबे स्वरूप - राम - राय, करि’ नाना उपाय
महाप्रभुर करे आश्वासन ।
गायेन सङ्गम - गीत, प्रभुर फिराइला चित
प्रभुर किछु स्थिर हैल मन ॥54॥
cc-antya-19.54.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya then devised various means to pacify the Lord. They sang songs of meeting that transformed His heart and made His mind peaceful.

devanagari: एइ - मत विलपिते अर्ध - रात्रि गेल ।
गम्भीराते स्वरूप - गोसाञि प्रभुरे शोयाइल ॥55॥
cc-antya-19.55.translation: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented in this way, half the night passed. Then Svarūpa Dāmodara made the Lord lie down in the room known as the Gambhīrā.

devanagari: प्रभुरे शोयाञा रामानन्द गेला घरे ।
स्वरूप, गोविन्द शुइला गम्भीरार द्वारे ॥56॥
cc-antya-19.56.translation: After the Lord was made to lie down, Rāmānanda Rāya returned home, and Svarūpa Dāmodara and Govinda lay down at the door of the Gambhīrā.

devanagari: प्रेमावेशे महाप्रभुर गर - गर मन ।
नाम - सङ्कीर्तन करि’ करेन जागरण ॥57॥
cc-antya-19.57.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed awake all night, chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, His mind overwhelmed by spiritual ecstasy.

devanagari: विरहे व्याकुल प्रभु उद्वेगे उठिला ।
गम्भीरार भित्त्ये मुख घषिते लागिला ॥58॥
cc-antya-19.58.translation: Feeling separation from Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was so distraught that in great anxiety He stood up and began rubbing His face against the walls of the Gambhīrā.

lines: mukhe, gaṇḍe, nāke kṣata ha-ila apāra
bhāvāveśe nā jānena prabhu, paḍe rakta-dhāra
devanagari: मुखे, गण्डे, नाके क्षत ह - इल अपार ।
भावावेशे ना जानेन प्रभु, पड़े रक्त - धार ॥59॥
cc-antya-19.59.translation: Blood oozed from the many injuries on His mouth, nose and cheeks, but due to His ecstatic emotions, the Lord did not know it.

devanagari: “नदीया चलह, मातारे कहिह नमस्कार ।
आमार नामे पाद - पद्म धरिह ताँहार ॥6॥
cc-antya-19.6.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, "Go to Nadia and offer My obeisances to My mother. Touch her lotus feet in My name.

devanagari: सर्व - रात्रि करेन भावे मुख सङ्घर्षण ।
गों - गों - शब्द करेन , - स्वरूप शुनिला तखन ॥60॥
cc-antya-19.60.translation: In ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rubbed His face against the walls all night long, making a peculiar sound, "goṅ-goṅ," which Svarūpa Dāmodara could hear through the door.

lines: dīpa jvāli' ghare gelā, dekhi' prabhura mukha
svarūpa, govinda duṅhāra haila baḍa duḥkha
devanagari: दीप ज्वालि’ घरे गेला, देखि’ प्रभुर मुख ।
स्वरूप, गोविन्द दुँहार हैल बड़ दुःख ॥61॥
cc-antya-19.61.translation: Lighting a lamp, Svarūpa Dāmodara and Govinda entered the room. When they saw the Lord's face, both of them were full of sorrow.

devanagari: प्रभुरे शय्याते आनि’ सुस्थिर कराइला ।
‘काँहे कैला एइ तुमि?’ - स्वरूप पुछिला ॥62॥
cc-antya-19.62.translation: They brought the Lord to His bed, calmed Him and then asked, "Why have You done this to Yourself?"

lines: prabhu kahena,—"udvege ghare nā pāri rahite
dvāra cāhi' buli' śīghra bāhira ha-ite
devanagari: प्रभु कहेन, - “उद्वेगे घरे ना पारि रहिते ।
द्वार चाहि’ बुलि’ शीघ्र बाहिर ह - इते ॥63॥
cc-antya-19.63.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I was in such anxiety that I could not stay in the room. I wanted to go out, and therefore I wandered about the room, looking for the door.

lines: dvāra nāhi' pāñā mukha lāge cāri-bhite
kṣata haya, rakta paḍe, nā pāi yāite"
devanagari: द्वार नाहि’ पाञा मुख लागे चारि - भिते ।
क्षत हय, रक्त पड़े, ना पाइ याइते” ॥64॥
cc-antya-19.64.translation: "Unable to find the door, I kept hitting the four walls with My face. My face was injured, and it bled, but I still could not get out."

devanagari: उन्माद - दशाय प्रभुर स्थिर नहे मन ।
येइ करे, येइ बोले सब , - उन्माद - लक्षण ॥65॥
cc-antya-19.65.translation: In this state of madness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind was unsteady. Whatever He said or did was all symptomatic of madness.

lines: bhakta-gaṇa lañā vicāra kailā āra dine
devanagari: स्वरूप - गोसाञि तबे चिन्ता पाइला मने ।
भक्त - गण ल ञा विचार कैला आर दिने ॥66॥
cc-antya-19.66.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara was very anxious, but then he had an idea. The following day, he and the other devotees considered it together.

lines: saba bhakta meli' tabe prabhure sādhila
devanagari: सब भक्त मेलि’ तबे प्रभुरे साधिल ।
शङ्कर - पण्डिते प्रभुर सङ्गे शोयाइल ॥67॥
cc-antya-19.67.translation: After consulting with one another, they entreated Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to allow Śaṅkara Paṇḍita to lie down in the same room with Him.

devanagari: प्रभु - पाद - तले शङ्कर करेन शयन ।
प्रभु ताँर उपर करेन पाद - प्रसारण ॥68॥
cc-antya-19.68.translation: Thus Śaṅkara Paṇḍita lay at the feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord placed His legs upon Śaṅkara's body.

devanagari: ‘प्रभु - पादोपाधा न’ बलि’ ताँर नाम ह - इल ।
पूर्वे विदुरे येन श्री - शुक वर्णिल ॥69॥
cc-antya-19.69.translation: Śaṅkara became celebrated by the name "the pillow of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu." He was like Vidura, as Śukadeva Gosvāmī previously described him.

lines: nitya āsi' āmi tomāra vandiye caraṇa
devanagari: कहिह ताँहारे ‘तुमि करह स्मरण ।
नित्य आ सि’ आमि तोमार वन्दिये चरण ॥7॥
cc-antya-19.7.translation: "Tell her for Me, 'Please remember that I come here every day and offer My respects to your lotus feet.

devanagari: इति ब्रुवाणं विदुरं विनीतं सहस्त्र - शीर्णश्चरणोपधानम् । प्रहृष्ट - रोमा भगवत्कथायां ।
प्रणीयमानो मुनिरभ्यचष्ट ॥70॥
cc-antya-19.70.translation: "When submissive Vidura, the resting place of the legs of Lord Kṛṣṇa, had thus spoken to Maitreya, Maitreya began speaking, his hair standing on end due to the transcendental pleasure of discussing topics concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa."

devanagari: शङ्कर करेन प्रभुर पाद - सम्वाहन ।
घुमाञा पड़ेन, तैछे करेन शयन ॥71॥
cc-antya-19.71.translation: Śaṅkara massaged the legs of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but while massaging he would fall asleep and thus lie down.

devanagari: उघाड़ - अङ्गे पड़िया शङ्कर निद्रा याय ।
प्रभु उठि’ आपन - काँथा ताहारे जड़ाय ॥72॥
cc-antya-19.72.translation: He would lie asleep without a covering on his body, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would get up and wrap him with His own quilt.

devanagari: निरन्तर घुमाय शङ्कर शीघ्र - चेतन ।
वसि’ पाद चापि’ करे रात्रि - जागरण ॥73॥
cc-antya-19.73.translation: Śaṅkara Paṇḍita would always fall asleep, but he would quickly awaken, sit up and again begin massaging the legs of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. In this way he would stay awake the entire night.

lines: tāṅra bhaye nārena prabhu bāhire yāite
tāṅra bhaye nārena bhittye mukhābja ghaṣite
devanagari: ताँर भये नारेन प्रभु बाहिरे याइते ।
ताँर भये नारेन भित्त्ये मुखाब्ज घषिते ॥74॥
cc-antya-19.74.translation: Out of fear of Śaṅkara, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could neither leave His room nor rub His lotuslike face against the walls.

devanagari: एइ लीला महाप्रभुर रघुनाथ - दास ।
गौराङ्ग - स्तव - कल्पवृक्षे करियाछे प्रकाश ॥75॥
cc-antya-19.75.translation: This pastime of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's has been described very nicely by Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī in his book known as Gaurāṅga-stava-kalpavṛkṣa.

lines: pralāpān unmādāt satatam ati kurvan vikala-dhīḥ
kṣātotthaṁ gaurāṅgo hṛdaya udayan māṁ madayati
devanagari: स्वकीयस्य प्राणार्बुद - सदृश - गोष्ठस्य विरहात् प्रलापानुन्मादात्सततमति कुर्वन्विकल - धीः ।
दधद्भित्तौ शश्वद्वदन - विधु - घर्षेण रुधिरं क्षतोत्थं गौराङ्गो हृदय उदयन्मां मदयति ॥76॥
cc-antya-19.76.translation: "Because of separation from His many friends in Vṛndāvana, who were like His own life, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke like a madman. His intelligence was transformed. Day and night He rubbed His moonlike face against the walls, and blood flowed from the injuries. May that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rise in my heart and make me mad with love."

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु रात्रि - दिवसे ।
प्रेम - सिन्धु - मग्न रहे, कभु डुबे, भासे ॥77॥
cc-antya-19.77.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in this way stayed immersed day and night in an ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. Sometimes He was submerged, and sometimes He floated.

devanagari: एक - काले वैशाखेर पौर्णमासी - दिने ।
रात्रि - काले महाप्रभु चलिला उद्याने ॥78॥
cc-antya-19.78.translation: One full-moon night in the month of Vaiśākha [April and May], Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to a garden.

devanagari: ‘जगन्नाथ - वल्लभ’ नाम उद्यान - प्रधाने ।
प्रवेश करिला प्रभु लञा भक्त - गणे ॥79॥
cc-antya-19.79.translation: The Lord, along with His devotees, entered one of the nicest gardens, called Jagannātha-vallabha.

devanagari: ये - दिने तोमार इच्छा कराइते भोजन ।
से - दिने आ सि’ अवश्य करिये भक्षण ॥8॥
cc-antya-19.8.translation: "Any day you desire to feed Me, I certainly come and accept what you offer.

lines: śuka, śārī, pika, bhṛṅga kare ālāpana
devanagari: प्रफुल्लित वृक्ष - वल्ली , - येन वृन्दावन ।
शुक, शारी, पिक, भृङ्ग करे आलापन ॥80॥
cc-antya-19.80.translation: In the garden were fully blossomed trees and creepers exactly like those in Vṛndāvana. Bumblebees and birds like the śuka, śārī and pika talked with one another.

devanagari: पुष्प - गन्ध लञा वहे मलय - पवन ।
‘गुरु’ हञा तरु - लताय शिखाय नाचन ॥81॥
cc-antya-19.81.translation: A mild breeze was blowing, carrying the fragrance of aromatic flowers. The breeze had become a guru and was teaching all the trees and creepers how to dance.

devanagari: पूर्ण - चन्द्र - चन्द्रिकाय परम उज्वल ।
तरु - लतादि ज्योत्स्नाय करे झलमल ॥82॥
cc-antya-19.82.translation: Brightly illuminated by the full moon, the trees and creepers glittered in the light.

devanagari: छय ऋतु - गण याहाँ वसन्त प्रधान ।
देखि’ आनन्दित हैला गौर भगवान् ॥83॥
cc-antya-19.83.translation: The six seasons, especially spring, seemed present there. Seeing the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was very happy.

lines: nṛtya kari' bulena prabhu nija-gaṇa lañā
devanagari: “ललित - लवङ्ग - लता” पद गाओया ञा ।
नृत्य करि’ बुलेन प्रभु निज - गण ल ञा ॥84॥
cc-antya-19.84.translation: In this atmosphere, the Lord had His associates sing a verse from the Gīta-govinda, beginning with the words "lalita-lavaṅga-latā," as He danced and wandered about with them.

devanagari: प्रति - वृक्ष - वल्ली ऐछे भ्रमिते भ्रमिते ।
अशोकेर तले कृष्णे देखेन आचम्बिते ॥85॥
cc-antya-19.85.translation: As He thus wandered around every tree and creeper, He came beneath an aśoka tree and suddenly saw Lord Kṛṣṇa.

lines: āge dekhi' hāsi' kṛṣṇa antardhāna ha-ilā
devanagari: कृष्ण देखि’ महाप्रभु धाञा चलिला ।
आगे दे खि’ हासि’ कृष्ण अन्तर्धान ह - इला ॥86॥
cc-antya-19.86.translation: When He saw Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began running very swiftly, but Kṛṣṇa smiled and disappeared.

lines: āge pāilā kṛṣṇe, tāṅre punaḥ hārāñā
devanagari: आगे पाइला कृष्णे, ताँरे पुनः हाराञा ।
भूमेते पड़िला प्रभु मूर्च्छित हञा ॥87॥
cc-antya-19.87.translation: Having first gotten Kṛṣṇa and then having lost Him again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell to the ground unconscious.

lines: sei gandha pāñā prabhu hailā acetane
devanagari: कृष्णेर श्री - अङ्ग - गन्धे भरिछे उद्याने ।
सेइ गन्ध पाञा प्रभु हैला अचेतने ॥88॥
cc-antya-19.88.translation: The entire garden was filled with the scent of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body. When Srī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smelled it, He fell unconscious at once.

devanagari: निरन्तर नासाय पशे कृष्ण - परिमल ।
गन्ध आस्वादिते प्रभु ह - इला पागल ॥89॥
cc-antya-19.89.translation: The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body, however, incessantly entered His nostrils, and the Lord became mad to relish it.

lines: tomāra sevā chāḍi' āmi kariluṅ sannyāsa
devanagari: तोमार सेवा छा ड़ि’ आमि करि लुँ सन्यास ।
‘बाउल’ हञा आमि कैलुँ धर्म - नाश ॥9॥
cc-antya-19.9.translation: “ 'I have given up service to you and have accepted the vow of sannyāsa. I have thus become mad and have destroyed the principles of religion.

lines: sei śloka paḍi' prabhu artha karilā
devanagari: कृष्ण - गन्ध - लुब्धा राधा सखीरे ये कहिला ।
सेइ श्लोक प ड़ि’ प्रभु अर्थ करिला ॥90॥
cc-antya-19.90.translation: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī expressed to Her gopī friends how She hankers for the transcendental scent of Kṛṣṇa's body. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited that same verse and made its meaning clear.

lines: sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti nāsā-spṛhām
devanagari: कुरङ्ग - मद - जिद्वपुः - परिमलोर्मि - कृष्टाङ्गनः स्वकाङ्ग - नलिना ष्टके शशि - युताब्ज - गन्ध - प्रथः ।
मदेन्दुवर - चन्दनागुरु - सुगन्धि - चर्चार्चितः स मे मदन - मोहनः सखि तनोति नासा - स्पृहाम् ॥91॥
cc-antya-19.91.translation: “ 'The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body surpasses the aroma of musk and attracts the minds of all women. The eight lotuslike parts of His body distribute the fragrance of lotuses mixed with that of camphor. His body is anointed with aromatic substances like musk, camphor, sandalwood and aguru. O My dear friend, that Personality of Godhead, also known as the enchanter of Cupid, always increases the desire of My nostrils.'

devanagari: कस्तूरिका - नीलोत्पल, तार येइ परिमल
ताहा जि नि’ कृष्ण - अङ्ग - गन्ध ।
व्यापे चौद्द - भुवने, करे सर्व आकर्षणे
नारी - गणेर आङ्घि करे अन्ध ॥92॥
cc-antya-19.92.translation: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body surpasses the fragrances of musk and the bluish lotus flower. Spreading throughout the fourteen worlds, it attracts everyone and makes the eyes of all women blind.

lines: nārīra nāsāte paśe, sarva-kāla tāhāṅ vaise,
devanagari: सखि हे, कृष्ण - गन्ध जगत्माताय
नारीर नासाते पशे, सर्व - काल ताहाँ वैसे, ।
कृष्ण - पाश ध रि’ लञा याय ॥93॥
cc-antya-19.93.translation: "My dear friend, the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body enchants the entire world. It especially enters the nostrils of women and remains seated there. Thus it captures them and forcibly brings them to Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: नेत्र - नाभि, वदन, कर - युग चरण ,
एइ अष्ट - पद्म कृष्ण - अङ्गे ।
कर्पूर - लिप्त कमल, तार यैछे परिमल ,
सेइ गन्ध अष्ट - पद्म - सङ्गे ॥94॥
cc-antya-19.94.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's eyes, navel and face, hands and feet are like eight lotus flowers on His body. From those eight lotuses emanates a fragrance like a mixture of camphor and lotus. That is the scent associated with His body.

lines: karpūra-sane carcā aṅge, pūrva aṅgera gandha saṅge,
devanagari: हेम - कीलित चन्दन, ताहा क रि’ घर्षण ,
ताहे अगुरु, कुङ्कम, कस्तूरी ।
कर्पूर - सने चर्चा अङ्गे, पूर्व अङ्गेर गन्ध सङ्गे,
मिलि’ तारे येन कैल चुरि ॥95॥
cc-antya-19.95.translation: "When sandalwood pulp with aguru, kuṅkuma and musk is mixed with camphor and spread on Kṛṣṇa's body, it combines with Kṛṣṇa's own original bodily perfume and seems to cover it.

lines: hare nārīra tanu-mana, nāsā kare ghūrṇana,
devanagari: हरे नारीर तनु - मन, नासा करे घूर्णन,
खसाय नीवि, छुटाय केश - बन्ध ।
करिया आगे बाउरी, नाचाय जगत् नारी,
हेन डाकातिया कृष्णाङ्ग - गन्ध ॥96॥
cc-antya-19.96.translation: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body is so attractive that it enchants the bodies and minds of all women. It bewilders their nostrils, loosens their belts and hair, and makes them madwomen. All the women of world come under its influence, and therefore the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body is like a plunderer.

lines: sei gandha-vaśa nāsā, sadā kare gandhera āśā,
pāile piyā peṭa bhare, piṅa piṅa tabu kare,
devanagari: सेइ गन्ध - वश नासा, सदा करे गन्धेर आशा ,
कभु पाय, कभु नाहि पाय ।
पाइले पिया पेट भरे, पिङपिङतबु करे,
ना पाइले तृष्णाय मरि’ याय ॥97॥
cc-antya-19.97.translation: "Falling completely under its influence, the nostrils yearn for it continuously, although sometimes they obtain it and sometimes not. When they do they drink their fill, though they still want more and more, but if they don't, out of thirst they die.

lines: vinā-mūlye deya gandha, gandha diyā kare andha,
devanagari: मदन - मोहन - नाट, पसारि गन्धेर हाट
जगन्नारी - ग्राहके लोभाय ।
